a200.speaker: H.E. Moses Micheal Engadu, AMSG Secretary-General
a200.speech: “Our critical minerals are the foundation of global sustainable development and the catalyst for Africa’s industrialization,” said Engadu, stressing the importance of harmonized policies, capital mobilization, and transparent global partnerships that directly benefit African citizens.

a200.speaker: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu of Nigeria, represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima
a200.speech: At the inaugural UNGA sideline meeting in 2024, emphasized that Africa, with its vast mineral wealth, can achieve self-sufficiency without reliance on foreign aid.

a200.speaker: Core International, represented by Managing Partner Suleiman Zakari
a200.speech: Reaffirmed its commitment, calling the roundtable “a chance to move from dialogue to results.”

a310.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a310.speech: Announced on Friday that Elon Musk is preparing to intervene in the education and defence sectors, stating at a White House press conference that he had instructed Musk “to go and look into education, to go and look at the Pentagon, that is to say, the military.”

a310.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a310.speech: Asked about the limits of Musk's action, mentioned “perhaps the areas of very high security,” but insisted that the billionaire was surrounded by “a group of very qualified people” and knew what he was doing.

a310.speaker: Elon Musk, head of DOGE / billionaire entrepreneur
a310.speech: Said on X that “American weapons programmes needed to be completely reviewed.”

a310.speaker: Elon Musk, head of DOGE / billionaire entrepreneur
a310.speech: Wrote on X, targeting the consumer protection agency: “RIP CFPB,” accompanied by a tombstone emoji.

a310.speaker: Elon Musk, head of DOGE / billionaire entrepreneur
a310.speech: Displayed his support for the president by writing: “I love Donald Trump as much as a straight man can love another man.”

a348.speaker: Duncan Harvey, Country Director, Save the Children International (SCI) Nigeria
a348.speech: Raised alarm over the worsening situation in the country, stating that the combination of catastrophic climate disasters, escalating insecurity, and soaring prices has pushed the crisis to unprecedented levels; emphasized that these factors are threatening the livelihoods of over 16 million children, leaving them at risk of hunger ; "In Nigeria, the crisis is reaching unprecedented levels as catastrophic climate disasters, escalating insecurity, and soaring prices threaten to leave over 16 million children hungry. Urgent action is essential to combat this devastating and unacceptable trend of child hunger and malnutrition and ensure a brighter future for Nigeria's children."

a348.speaker: Duncan Harvey, Country Director, Save the Children International (SCI) Nigeria
a348.speech: "Save the Children is calling on governments to address food insecurity by tackling food shortages, stabilize rising prices, and increase protection for farmers facing violence from armed groups." ; "Governments also need to address the climate crisis by building communities' resilience, as well as more awareness and early warning for people to prepare for climate induced disasters," Harvey said on Tuesday.

a348.speaker: Save the Children International (SCI) forecast
a348.speech: An alarming forecast from SCI revealing that an additional one million children are expected to suffer from acute malnutrition by April next year; saying that urgent action is needed to prevent further suffering and loss of life.

a348.speaker: Cadre Harmonise analysis (leading authority on hunger in the Sahel and West Africa)
a348.speech: The latest analysis has raised alarming concerns over the rising levels of food insecurity in Nigeria; according to the data, 5.4 million Nigerian children are now at risk of suffering from acute malnutrition by April 2024, a 25% increase compared to 4.4 million children at risk last year; the report further highlights that of these 5.4 million children, approximately 1.8 million could face Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM), a life-threatening condition.

a348.speaker: United Nations
a348.speech: In 2020, the United Nations estimated that 7% of the Nigerian population faced hunger, but the figure has now risen to 15%.

a462.speaker: Justice James Alala, presiding judge in the trial of Dr Riek Machar
a462.speech: Issued a stern set of ground rules to maintain order and discipline in the courtroom, emphasizing that while the law guarantees a public trial, all attendees—including the media—have a duty to ensure peace during the proceedings, and making it clear that a failure to comply would result in immediate removal ; “The law provides for public trial, meaning that the court is open to everybody. However, the public has a duty to keep peace in the courtroom,” Justice Alala stated. ; “Therefore, there is a need to comply with the following… send away any media apparatus or any person who fails to observe the above requirements and may decide to go for close proceedings or take legal measures against anyone who is not able to adhere to the law.” ; The judge stressed that these measures are essential to preserve a serious and respectful environment for the trial.

a469.speaker: Ukraine Support Tracker
a469.speech: According to the Ukraine Support Tracker, since the war began through mid-2025, Europe allocated €35.1bn in military aid via new procurement contracts—€4.4bn more than the U.S. over the same period.

a469.speaker: Brookings
a469.speech: According to Brookings, Europe is positioning itself to become the main Western backer of Ukraine once U.S. attention recedes.

a469.speaker: Scott Ritter, military analyst (opinion piece published by Sputnik)
a469.speech: Argues Europe has deliberately stoked conflict in order to justify defense expansion, marginalize Russia, and tie Ukraine permanently to European structures. He asserts: “Europe used Ukraine as its proxy to fight and weaken Russia… Europe did not negotiate the Minsk agreements in good faith… Europe continues to provide Ukraine with weapons and cash.”

a469.speaker: Reuters Breakingviews column
a469.speech: Notes that while Europe has money, it often lacks the military hardware to match its financial commitment and sometimes must purchase U.S. systems to fill gaps.

a469.speaker: SIPRI
a469.speech: Notes that Europe’s arms exports to Ukraine and collaborative defense production are shifting longstanding norms, requiring regulatory overhaul.

a495.speaker: Pr Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
a495.speech: In her introductory remarks, stressed the commitment of the Government of Niger to all the initiatives put in place to guarantee security. She also recalled the importance of this day, which honours the memory of the humanitarian workers who were victims of the attack on the United Nations house on 19 August 2003 in Baghdad, and the praiseworthy actions carried out by them to save and improve the lives of many people, as well as the importance of community participation in achieving the predefined objectives. "Humanitarian aid accompanies, but it is the communities that initiate, guide and shape the responses to their challenges. It is important to respect dignity, beyond relief, because it is the women, the men and the children who resist crises every day," she said. By supporting projects arising from community-led initiatives, she added, collective resilience and appropriate responses are built in connection with government action.

a495.speaker: Pr Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
a495.speech: Stressed that terrorist acts constitute a brake on Niger's development, forcing many people to live in conditions of high precariousness and thereby accentuating forced displacement, epidemics, malnutrition, floods, social psychosis and food insecurity in several areas of the country and in the AES Confederation area.

a495.speaker: Kinday Samba, interim Humanitarian Coordinator
a495.speech: Explained that the choice of this year's theme is a call to decision-makers to use their position and influence to put an end to human atrocities, relying on human rights legal instruments, international humanitarian law and all available means. She also mentioned the missions assigned to humanitarian workers and their concrete impact on the lives of local communities. "Through this day, we aspire to continue advocacy for the protection of civilians and humanitarian workers, to promote respect for international humanitarian law and for the principles that guide humanitarian action," she said. She also mentioned the importance of humanitarian workers, which consists in relieving suffering, strengthening community resilience and fostering sustainable responses guided by the real needs of the populations.

a495.speaker: Kinday Samba, interim Humanitarian Coordinator
a495.speech: Noted that the humanitarian situation in Niger remains worrying despite all the efforts made by the authorities, because of the violence perpetrated in the three-borders area, generating additional humanitarian needs.

a495.speaker: Kinday Samba, interim Humanitarian Coordinator
a495.speech: Stresses that several advances have been recorded thanks to humanitarian aid combined with government efforts, notably better control of the impact of floods thanks to preventive measures put in place, an improvement in the food and nutrition situation thanks to the availability of cereals on the market, moderate-price sales operations and the positive impact of the vast irrigation campaign. She praised the efforts of the authorities, who continue to establish a climate of security and peace allowing the various operations to be carried out and challenges to be met. "This requires increased mobilisation, a strengthened commitment from all stakeholders. Anticipatory actions can help prevent natural disasters, because acting before a foreseeable shock is not only more effective but also less costly than the traditional humanitarian response. We must promote sustainable solutions for greater community self-reliance," she suggested.

a495.speaker: Mme Lafuente Nena, Representative of the Technical and Financial Partners
a495.speech: Praised the noble and constant work of humanitarian workers to save the lives of vulnerable people, often at the expense of their own. "In 2024, 383 humanitarian workers were killed, compared with 265 humanitarian workers who lost their lives in 2025," she lamented. She then launched an appeal to all parties to guarantee the protection and security of civilians and humanitarian workers. "On this day, let us commit to protecting our workers and all act for humanity," she maintained.

a495.speaker: M. Issoufou Soumana, Representative of national and international NGOs
a495.speech: Praised the noble and constant work of humanitarian workers to save the lives of vulnerable people, often at the expense of their own ; recalled the constant effort of NGOs to mobilise funds in order to continuously assist millions of people in Niger despite the challenges they face. He also reaffirmed the commitment of NGOs alongside the populations and the Government to preserve human dignity and strengthen the resilience of communities.

a638.speaker: Government of Cabo Verde (official notice/edital)
a638.speech: Announced that it will prepare a programme to attract international technological startups wishing to expand into new markets.

a638.speaker: World Bank
a638.speech: Considered Cabo Verde's development model exhausted, in a year in which Cabo Verde was one of the fastest-growing economies in sub-Saharan Africa.

a638.speaker: President of the Technology Park of Cabo Verde institution
a638.speech: Said the first companies begin operating this month in the Technology Park of Cabo Verde, in Praia, considered the “heart” of the country's digital strategy, whose inauguration is scheduled for the end of the year.

a638.speaker: Businesspeople in Cabo Verde's technology sector
a638.speech: Say that the reality of the digital economy is still far from the theory.

a638.speaker: Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a638.speech: Said the Government intends to create a Special Technological Economic Zone in the city of Praia that includes the Technology Park, which should be ready next year.

a868.speaker: German government
a868.speech: Said yesterday that Israel’s decision to halt aid deliveries and cut off the electricity supply to Gaza could prompt a fresh humanitarian crisis in the Palestinian territory.

a868.speaker: Kathrin Deschauer, German foreign ministry spokeswoman
a868.speech: Told a regular press conference Gaza was “again threatened with a food shortage” ; “We note with great concern the cutting off of electricity and the discussion about stopping the water supply.” ; “Such steps are or would be unacceptable and incompatible with (Israel’s) obligations under international law.” ; said Germany “calls on the Israeli government to lift restrictions for all forms of humanitarian aid to Gaza with immediate effect.”

a868.speaker: Hamas
a868.speech: Accused Israel of reneging on the ceasefire deal, saying in a statement Monday Israel “refuses to commence the second phase, exposing its intentions of evasion and stalling.”

a868.speaker: Media reports
a868.speech: Said a top official from the domestic security agency Shin Bet will lead Israel’s delegation.

a868.speaker: Eli Cohen, Israeli Energy Minister
a868.speech: “We will use all the tools at our disposal to bring back the hostages and ensure that Hamas is no longer in Gaza the day after” the war, said as he ordered the power cut.

a868.speaker: Abdul Latif al-Qanoua, Hamas spokesman
a868.speech: Said Israel’s move will impact its hostages still held in Gaza ; “The decision to cut electricity is a failed option and poses a threat to its (Israeli) prisoners, who will only be freed through negotiations,” said in a statement yesterday.

a868.speaker: Izzat al-Rishq, top Hamas official
a868.speech: Called Israel’s decision “to cut off electricity to Gaza, after depriving it of food, medicine, and water” a “desperate attempt to pressure our people and their resistance.”

a1127.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), on X
a1127.speech: Announced last Monday the imminent closure of USAID and wrote on his social network X (formerly Twitter): "USAID is a criminal organization and a nest of vipers of radical left-wing Marxists who hate America. It is time for it to disappear. With Donald Trump's blessing, we are shutting down the agency."

a1127.speaker: Several observers and experts
a1127.speech: Questioned the legality of the closure of the development agency and of placing it under supervision. For them it is an arbitrary decision, even an abuse of power on the part of the new occupant of the White House — a decision which, according to them, not only benefits the country's adversaries, but whose implementation by decree is purely illegal.

a1127.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State and acting director of USAID
a1127.speech: Justifies this takeover by a lack of transparency over USAID's funding, citing internal insubordination, and assures that certain missions will be maintained despite the closure.

a1127.speaker: Community of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) countries
a1127.speech: In their eyes this closure is a good thing, and they even thank Donald Trump for it. For them, the closure of this agency will have no consequence; on the contrary, they consider that USAID supports destabilization operations on the continent, notably in the Sahel countries, specifically within the AES.

a1127.speaker: A Nigerien (anonymous)
a1127.speech: "Without the support of this American aid agency, terrorist groups such as the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara or Iyad Ag Ghaly's JNIM could find themselves short of weapons, ammunition and reconnaissance means. This is one of the very good pieces of news for Africa, because USAID is an unconventional weapon of war for American special forces, who use psychological manipulation methods and support insurrection and irregular warfare against Africans."

a1216.speaker: Ayotade Oyinlola, Executive Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer, IHS Nigeria
a1216.speech: Listed the company's giant strides, including its consistent investments in state-of-the-art communication infrastructure and world-class services that have put Nigeria on a very strong footing in the global telecommunication market ; said at the time, that in an era where connectivity serves as the lifeblood of societies and economies, IHS Towers stands as a beacon of success, demonstrating how a company that was established in Nigeria, in a little over two decades (2001), has grown to become a reckonable multinational telecom infrastructure powerhouse, with footprints in 11 countries across three continents and impacting the lives of over 800 million people.

a1216.speaker: IHS Nigeria senior management team
a1216.speech: Asserted that the company, despite having an expansive global footprint, including a remarkable global tower count of over 40,000 towers across Nigeria, Brazil, Cameroon, Colombia, Côte d'Ivoire, Egypt, Kuwait, Peru, Rwanda, South Africa and Zambia, proudly maintains its Nigerian identity.

a1216.speaker: Kazeem Oladepo, Chief Operating Officer, IHS Nigeria
a1216.speech: Reeled out the company's numerous interventions, including investments in school connectivity. He said IHS has unveiled ICT and digital infrastructures aimed at promoting Nigeria's digital economy, which include the innovation hub at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology (LAUTECH), Ogbomoso, in collaboration with the Oyo state government, and a three-year partnership with the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation, and Digital Economy in support of the government's Three Million Technical Talent (3MTT) Initiative.

a1216.speaker: Kazeem Oladepo, Chief Operating Officer, IHS Nigeria
a1216.speech: Underscored the company's pivotal role in lowering barriers to entry for mobile network and internet service providers, catalysing infrastructure development, and fostering innovation hubs across Nigeria. He further shared IHS Towers' illustrious journey from its inception in Lagos, in 2001, to its becoming a global powerhouse with footprints in 11 markets across three continents. He also stated that the IHS was the first Nigerian-rooted company to be publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), in 2021.

a1216.speaker: Biodun Oyebanji, Ekiti State Governor
a1216.speech: Led the voices that showcased Nigeria's burgeoning investment opportunities during the session on "Invest in Nigeria: Showcasing Investment Opportunities."

a1216.speaker: Yusuf Maitama Tuggar, Nigerian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1216.speech: Affirmed Nigeria's commitment to strengthening bilateral relations and strategic partnerships aimed at stimulating foreign direct investments inflow to Nigeria.

a1216.speaker: IHS Nigeria, represented by Dapo Otunla, Chief Corporate Services Officer
a1216.speech: Reaffirmed its unwavering commitment to propelling sustainable industrial growth across the continent; the company reiterated that it was dedicated to infrastructure investment, technology adoption, and collaborative partnerships as key drivers of Africa's industrial revolution.

a1216.speaker: Yemi Osinbajo, former Vice President of Nigeria and Guardian of Timbuktoo African Innovation Foundation
a1216.speech: Highlighted the importance of innovation and technology in driving industrial growth.

a1308.speaker: Eric Mabuza Jnr, General Manager, ITHUBA Uganda (opinion column)
a1308.speech: Writes that when the Uganda National Lottery was launched a few months ago, “we didn't simply introduce a game. We introduced a promise—a promise of fairness, opportunity, and national progress. And today, I can confidently say: that promise is already coming to life.” ; Says at ITHUBA the mission has never been just about creating winners but about creating impact, and that what excites him most is that “this transformation is funded not by debt or foreign aid—but by Ugandans themselves. Every UGX 600 DAILY LOTTO ticket or UGX 1,000 POWERBALL play becomes a small act of nation-building.” ; Says he has witnessed firsthand how a National Lottery can drive real, measurable development, noting ITHUBA has channelled more than $650 million from ticket sales into good causes over the past decade ; Says the company has invested heavily in systems that ensure integrity, that every game is fully digital and operations are 100% regulated by the NLGRB, and that ITHUBA encourages responsible gaming and has partnered with counselling organisations ; Says jobs have been created, small businesses are benefiting and communities are gaining access to new resources: “This is what it looks like when a National Lottery becomes more than entertainment. It becomes an economic engine.” ; “So, the next time you buy a ticket, know that you're not just playing for a chance to win. You're joining a movement—one that's transforming communities, supporting dreams, and building a better Uganda.”

a1308.speaker: National Lotteries and Gaming Regulatory Board (NLGRB)
a1308.speech: Has already identified the upcoming AFCON 2027 tournament as a flagship beneficiary of Uganda National Lottery proceeds, supporting the construction of world-class stadiums and training facilities.

a1431.speaker: Authorities of the University of Burundi
a1431.speech: The authorities state that breakfast was making students lazy, so that they began dozing off from the first hour of class.

a1431.speaker: Unofficial sources at the university / an authorised source at the Mutanga campus (anonymous)
a1431.speech: According to unofficial sources at the university, the elimination of breakfast was also decided in order to fight obesity, which is constantly increasing at the university. "Many students are overweight," says an authorised source at the Mutanga campus.

a1431.speaker: Talk in the corridors of the rectorate (anonymous)
a1431.speech: "Digestion prevents thinking, reflecting. Students deprived of breakfast will follow their courses better," is what is said in the corridors of the rectorate.

a1431.speaker: World Health Organization
a1431.speech: This decision was welcomed by the World Health Organization, and a large delegation led by the institution's Director-General is expected in Bujumbura in the coming days.

a1431.speaker: University of Burundi (official position)
a1431.speech: "The whole world is following our decision closely. In the United States, in France, everywhere, universities want to take the same measure. The University of Burundi is delighted to be at the forefront of progress." ; The university asserts that this elimination of breakfast has nothing to do with "economic problems" - "it is a question of public health."

a1431.speaker: International Union of Nutritionists and Dieticians (communiqué)
a1431.speech: In a communiqué, welcomed the measure and hopes that other universities around the world will imitate the determination of the Burundian rectoral authorities.

a1431.speaker: President of the students' association
a1431.speech: Declared that this elimination "is a machete blow" in the back of the students.

a1431.speaker: University of Burundi rectorate
a1431.speech: "When a revolutionary measure is taken there are always reactionary forces," the rectorate says dismissively; explanatory sessions will be given to demonstrate "the benefits of morning fasting"; the rectorate wants students without excess weight.

a1477.speaker: Tleetse Phakoe, Executive Director of Women Initiatives Lesotho (WIL), 2025 Mandela Washington Fellow at Texas Tech University
a1477.speech: "I am here learning systems of public management from every angle and every aspect," she explains, "so that I can navigate ways of localizing these systems for Lesotho, where public systems are not always well-defined at the community level."

a1477.speaker: Tleetse Phakoe, Executive Director of Women Initiatives Lesotho (WIL)
a1477.speech: "Success demands overcoming obstacles," stated Phakoe, highlighting a universal truth ; on self-doubt as a major personal hurdle: "When trying to establish WIL, first, I did not believe I could do it. I did not believe I could start or secure the necessary support to keep the organization running, given the current economy."

a1477.speaker: Tleetse Phakoe, Executive Director of Women Initiatives Lesotho (WIL)
a1477.speech: emphasises a critical gap: accessible funding for grassroots movements. "There are simply not enough grants out there that grassroots movements or smaller organizations can actually access," Phakoe explained. "Current grant demands often require significant existing financial resources. Many small organizations aren't even formally registered. They lack the capacity to source funds effectively, and it's clear they struggle to manage the grants they do get or qualify for the ones they need." ; "We cannot access the large grants needed to scale our impact to the level we aim for. We are building our profile; with time, we will reach a stage where we can handle larger grants and significantly scale our grassroots work."

a1477.speaker: Tleetse Phakoe, Executive Director of Women Initiatives Lesotho (WIL)
a1477.speech: said that "the withdrawal of USAID from Lesotho has also affected many other institutions providing funding, including private funders. This has shrunk the available funding pool, making it notably harder to secure grants."

a1477.speaker: Tleetse Phakoe, Executive Director of Women Initiatives Lesotho (WIL)
a1477.speech: on WIL's initiatives: "These trainings have directly benefited a staggering 300 women and their families," Phakoe reported ; "Our tree planting initiatives are the most impactful," she continued with pride. "The 'Green Mafeteng' initiative, in partnership with the Rural Women's Assembly, has collectively planted over 500 000 trees to date."

a1866.speaker: Cergio Lema, 50-year-old Ecuadoran cocoa farmer in Milagro
a1866.speech: Told AFP that a few years ago the price of cocoa "was so low you could only earn enough for the upkeep of the farm" ; "I have the vision of saving some money, taking out a loan, and buying another plot of land."

a1866.speaker: Marco Vasquez, 42-year-old cocoa farmer in Los Rios province
a1866.speech: Told AFP in a telephone call: "With the previous prices, it was impossible to invest, but now I've bought more seeds and constructed a small bridge to cross the stream that used to flood the plantations."

a1866.speaker: Ivan Ontaneda, president of Ecuadoran cocoa exporters group Anecacao
a1866.speech: "The current prosperity is no accident; we are reaping the benefits of years of private investment and research into a resilient variety."

a1866.speaker: Anecacao (Ecuadoran cocoa exporters group)
a1866.speech: Estimates that around 400,000 producers and exporters have benefitted from the price surge.

a1866.speaker: Ecuadoran agriculture ministry
a1866.speech: According to its agriculture ministry, Ecuador is the world's third-largest producer of the so-called "food of the gods."

a1866.speaker: Ecuador central bank
a1866.speech: According to the central bank, between September 2024 and March 2025 the value of cocoa exports surpassed those of bananas, of which Ecuador is the world's top exporter, for the first time in six decades.

a1866.speaker: Experts
a1866.speech: Have linked the heavy rains and extreme drought that wiped out African cocoa crops to climate change.

a1866.speaker: Environmental groups
a1866.speech: Have repeatedly warned of rampant deforestation related to cocoa production.

a1866.speaker: European Commission
a1866.speech: In May kept Ecuador off its highly anticipated first list of countries at "high risk" for deforestation.

a1874.speaker: Ahmed Aldikhari, MSF representative in Nigeria
a1874.speech: said in a statement: "We are witnessing massive budget cuts, particularly by the United States, the United Kingdom and the European Union, which are having a real impact on the treatment of malnourished children."

a1874.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) (press statement)
a1874.speech: warned that the number of minors with nutritional oedema, the most severe and lethal form of malnutrition, "has increased by 208% compared with the same period in 2024" ; "Since the beginning of 2025, 652 children have already died in our facilities due to the lack of timely access to health care," reads the statement released on Friday; from the start of the year to the end of June some 70,000 malnourished children received medical care from MSF teams in Katsina, including nearly 10,000 hospitalised in serious condition.

a1874.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a1874.speech: warned on Wednesday that it will suspend all of its emergency food and nutritional aid for 1.3 million people in north-eastern Nigeria at the end of July, due to a "critical shortage" of funding; the humanitarian agency also recalled that in the conflict-affected northern regions the resurgence of violence by jihadist groups — Boko Haram and, since 2016, its offshoot ISWAP — is causing mass displacement.

a1874.speaker: David Stevenson, WFP director in Nigeria
a1874.speech: said almost 31 million people in the country are currently facing acute hunger, an "unprecedented" number.

a1874.speaker: World Bank (data cited)
a1874.speech: According to the World Bank, four out of ten Nigerians live below the poverty line.

a1906.speaker: Chantal Boloia, Representative of OCHA
a1906.speech: Said that this workshop would make it possible to assess and to collaborate in determining the way forward with regard to the localisation agenda: "OCHA particularly supports this initiative because it is one of the main organisations advocating in favour of localisation."

a1906.speaker: Chantal Boloia, Representative of OCHA
a1906.speech: Said that between 2022 and 2023 the eligibility process for organisations able to submit projects at the national forum rose from 9 to 15, and that in 2024 assessments were carried out and other NGOs were made eligible ; explained: "Other efforts are being made to strengthen consortia in order to foster partnerships between international and national non-governmental organisations, thus offering more opportunities to local and national NGOs to benefit from funding and above all from capacity building. In 2023, 30% of the funding allocated through the regional fund was directly awarded to national and local NGOs."

a1906.speaker: Alhousseini Ahmidou, President of the Synergy of National Non-Governmental Organisations for Humanitarian Action (SONAH)
a1906.speech: Stressed that localisation has become a central theme of humanitarian aid in recent years, and that since the Grand Bargain commitments, and particularly over the last two years in West and Central Africa, several initiatives have been launched to improve and accelerate the place and role of national actors in humanitarian interventions ; declared: "In the absence of clearly defined objectives and exhaustive quantitative data on localisation, it is difficult to monitor national and international commitments, to estimate progress on localisation and to identify the remaining steps to be taken. This situation today constitutes a major obstacle to concrete advances in the field of localisation."

a1906.speaker: Alhousseini Ahmidou, President of the Synergy of National Non-Governmental Organisations for Humanitarian Action (SONAH)
a1906.speech: Stressed that for this first phase the programme targets eight countries of the West and Central Africa region: Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Chad and the Democratic Republic of Congo ; concluded: "The main contributor of funds is BHA-USAID, as well as NORCAP for some of the Lake Chad basin countries and the Hilton Foundation for Mali."

a1956.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) (statement)
a1956.speech: Said on Wednesday that living conditions for refugees in Ethiopia’s Gambella region are rapidly deteriorating following significant cuts to humanitarian aid in the region. ”The sharp decline is largely due to global reductions in support from key donors such as USAID, straining basic services such as food distribution, healthcare, access to clean water, and sanitation services”, MSF said in a statement.

a1956.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a1956.speech: Said nutrition services in four out of seven refugee camps have been stopped, putting 80,000 children under five at risk of life-threatening malnutrition; that since October 2024 refugees in Kule camp have received as little as 600 calories a day – less than 30 percent of the recommended daily minimum of 2,100 calories per person; and that so far in 2025 MSF has recorded a 55 percent increase in child admissions to its therapeutic feeding centre compared to the previous year, with half of these children coming from other camps in the region.

a1956.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a1956.speech: ”We urge humanitarian organisations and the Ethiopian authorities to scale up support and strengthen the healthcare system”.

a1956.speaker: Nyauahial Puoch, a mother who travelled about eight kilometres from Tierkidi refugee camp to seek treatment for her 17-month-old daughter at MSF’s facility in Kule camp
a1956.speech: “We receive food once a month—maize, wheat, and sorghum—but it always runs out before the month ends” ; “Since last year, there has been a big decline. Some of the items we used to get are no longer provided at all.”

a2095.speaker: Ministry of Health of Mozambique
a2095.speech: Says there is an increase of cases in some provinces due to the cut in international funding to the health sector.

a2095.speaker: Ivan Manhiça, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Health of Mozambique
a2095.speech: Explained that the disease is considered a public health problem in the country, since each year it is responsible for the deaths of thousands of people: "Mozambique continues to face a high burden of this disease, often associated with HIV, affecting mainly the most vulnerable populations, requiring coordinated actions, continuous investment and technological innovations for early diagnosis and effective treatment."

a2095.speaker: Benedita José, National head of the Tuberculosis Control Programme
a2095.speech: Explained: "Looking at the incidence in the general population, there are 361 per 100,000 inhabitants. With the real estimates we expect to find about 121,000 cases of tuberculosis per year."

a2095.speaker: Benedita José, National head of the Tuberculosis Control Programme
a2095.speech: Added the cut in international funding as the cause of the increase in cases in some provinces: "Some areas in certain provinces are beginning to record an increase in the number of cases, following the pace that existed before the interruption of USAID funding. We had a halt in the implementation of activities, which was one of the components that contributed most to [detecting] tuberculosis cases in health units. However, efforts are being made by the Ministry of Health to implement these activities using our multipurpose agents, who provide support in different areas."

a2095.speaker: Francisco Saúte, Director of the Manhiça Health Research Centre (CISM)
a2095.speech: Explained that the process is in the sample-collection phase: "I should first say that there is a tuberculosis vaccine, which is more than 100 years old, but it has limited efficacy in preventing infections. We are trialling a new one, using more recent technologies, and we are still in the initial evaluation phase and we are waiting for recruitment to be completed at all sites, so that the preliminary data analysis can be concluded."

a2151.speaker: Gerhard Erasmus, captain of the Richelieu Eagles
a2151.speech: Said the team representing Namibia at the ICC Men's T20 Cricket World Cup is well-balanced and raring to hit the ground running; said the squad has a good mixture of experience and young talent and that he is excited to lead the team at the World Cup.

a2151.speaker: Gerhard Erasmus, captain of the Richelieu Eagles
a2151.speech: Spoke highly of the youngsters who got the nod, saying that the inclusion of players such as PD Blignaut and Jack Brassell is about ensuring continuity; he said that the team is looking forward to testing themselves against some top cricket-playing nations like England and Australia.

a2151.speaker: Cricket Namibia
a2151.speech: Announced their 16-man Richelieu Eagles squad for the upcoming ICC Men's T20 Cricket World Cup set to be held in the USA and the West Indies.

a2186.speaker: Developing nations, including Malawi
a2186.speech: Are pushing for greater funding from rich nations most responsible for carbon emissions fuelling the climate crisis; are negotiating for quantifiable collective goals to reflect their needs and priorities.

a2186.speaker: African leaders and campaigners at CoP29
a2186.speech: Want money on the table, with wealthy nations pledging less than $700 million of the $400 billion low-income countries require to respond to climate-related disasters by 2030.

a2239.speaker: Daily Trust (editorial)
a2239.speech: "To declare that many Nigerians are hungry, suffering, and struggling to survive under hard economic conditions imposed by several economic factors, including record-high inflation rates is simply a restatement of the most obvious. While the terribly depleted purchasing power of the citizens continues to bite, the purported reduction of food prices has made little sense to millions of impoverished citizens as the all-season inflation continues to cripple micro and small-scale businesses; eating up entrepreneurs' hard-raised capitals." ; "Whether as entrepreneurs, low-income earners, or employers of labour, Nigerians as individuals or corporate entities are currently passing through difficult times. The hustling to meet up with their daily subsistence needs has put most family heads and homes under intense financial pressure. The comparatively worthless value of the naira has further turned most low-income earners into off-street beggars." ; "As direct or remote consequences of the burden of survival, starvation and malnutrition have since become threats to the health and survival of citizens including a large population of children particularly in some northern states of the country... We are already there." ; "President Donald Trump administration's cut to foreign aid is also a plausible factor. More life-threatening to the wellbeing of citizens is, indeed, the country's ailing economy."

a2239.speaker: Entrepreneurs and business owners (cited in the Daily Trust editorial)
a2239.speech: Reacting recently to the retention of interest rates at 27.5 per cent by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN)'s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), they "cried out that their businesses cannot survive on double digits' interest rate" and called on the CBN to come to the aid of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) by bringing down interest rates to single digits or by creating a special intervention fund for them.

a2239.speaker: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)
a2239.speech: Earlier in April 2025 had predicted that 33 million people in Nigeria including over 16 million children will not know where their next meal will come from in 2025.

a2239.speaker: Nutrition experts (cited in the Daily Trust editorial)
a2239.speech: Attribute the persistent malnutrition crisis in the northern region of the country to a variety of factors including inflation, food insecurity, insufficient healthcare infrastructure, cost of transportation, ongoing security challenges and disease outbreaks compounded by low vaccine coverage.

a2239.speaker: Tukur Muhammad-Baba, Publicity Secretary of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF)
a2239.speech: Noted on Arise Television that Nigerians were now suffering more under President Tinubu than they did during the administration of former President Goodluck Jonathan: "There's a lot of suffering under this present administration. At Jonathan's time, there was one major problem that was insecurity. He didn't have fuel subsidy. He left the naira alone. There was subsidy in electricity. All of these that have been removed have put the country now in a desperate situation and I think it's easy to say that people are suffering now more than they did but we need to put it in context... The removal of the fuel subsidy, removal of subsidy from electricity, the floating of the naira, all of these have amplified our problems."

a2239.speaker: Tukur Muhammad-Baba, Publicity Secretary of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF)
a2239.speech: Stated that the North had been neglected, and that all the problems affecting the region which the leaders discussed with Tinubu had not been addressed ; "The lopsided appointments into 'lucrative positions' by this government, the allocation of resources to one region of the country. So, you need to put all these into context but certainly the suffering that people are facing today and from north to south, from Sokoto to Akwa Ibom, from Lagos to Borno, affects everyone."

a2239.speaker: Tukur Muhammad-Baba, Publicity Secretary of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF)
a2239.speech: "I felt Goodluck Jonathan wasn't doing well, but I think that wasn't exactly what pushed him out. What pushed him out, in my opinion, were promises by the All-Progressives Congress (APC). One, anti-security. Two, anti-corruption. Three, development. None of these turned out that what we thought was the answer was far from being the answer." ; "Fast forward to 2023, the human being is a very hopeful and optimistic being. So, every time we elect people, support them, but I think it's not because they're north or south, it's because of what is on ground. For example, what will decide, in my opinion, the 2027 election is ability to respond to the people's needs."

a2239.speaker: The Presidency, in a statement by Sunday Dare, Special Adviser to the President on Media and Public Communications
a2239.speech: Argued that the nation's economic situation had been overstated by alarmists and subjective critics bent on creating confusion in the country, and pointed out that, contrary to the outlandish claims and portrayal of the country as a land of hunger, hardship and helplessness, Nigeria was speedily overcoming its difficulties ; "President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is not indifferent to Nigerians' difficulties. On the contrary, he is taking deliberate, targeted steps - many already yielding results - to reset our economy from a legacy of consumption without productivity, opacity without accountability, and policy that served the powerful, not the people."

a2239.speaker: The Presidency, in a statement by Sunday Dare, Special Adviser to the President on Media and Public Communications
a2239.speech: Frowned at the misinterpretation of the UNICEF prediction that 33 million Nigerians, including 16 million children, would face hunger this year, saying what was presented was not a UNICEF-specific report but the Cadre Harmonisé Food and Nutrition Insecurity Analysis, jointly prepared by the Federal Government of Nigeria, the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), the World Food Programme (WFP), and UNICEF: "It is not a current count, but a worst-case projection for the June-August 2025 lean season, assuming no mitigation actions by government or partners."

a2239.speaker: The Presidency, in a statement by Sunday Dare, Special Adviser to the President on Media and Public Communications
a2239.speech: Highlighted government's actions to avert the looming danger, including the release of over 42,000 metric tonnes of grains from federal strategic reserves, the procurement of an additional 117,000 metric tonnes, the reactivation of the Food Security Council by the President, and the scaling up of emergency nutrition support in Borno, Yobe, Adamawa, Katsina, Sokoto, and Bauchi states, noting that although malnutrition was a serious national concern, it should not be localised as a "Northern Nigeria" crisis ; "We also acknowledge that hardship is uneven across regions. However, Nigeria is one country, one people, and the fight against hunger is a collective effort, not a northern, southern, Christian, or Muslim issue. Since 2020, COVID has disrupted the global food system, worsened by the Russia-Ukraine war, and is now aggravated by conflict in the Middle East."

a2239.speaker: World Bank's April 2025 Food Security Update (report cited by the Presidency)
a2239.speech: According to it, over 1.4 billion people worldwide are under food stress, a problem that is not unique to Nigeria.

a2450.speaker: Davido, seven-year-old child at Nyamithuthu Camp
a2450.speech: “I drew my family in a car. I miss my home, but I am happy to be with friends here.”

a2450.speaker: Loyce, nine-year-old child at Nyamithuthu Camp
a2450.speech: “I drew a girl with a suitcase because we had to leave everything behind. I hope we can go back someday.”

a2450.speaker: Estere Tsoka, Unicef Malawi Emergency Specialist
a2450.speech: Emphasised the importance of these creative spaces in fostering healing, allowing children to process their trauma through play and expression: “The stories of Davido and Loyce are not just tales of survival but also of courage and creativity. As they continue to heal, their artwork serves as a powerful reminder that every child deserves a safe space to express themselves and dream of a better tomorrow.”

a2450.speaker: Estere Tsoka, Unicef Malawi Emergency Specialist
a2450.speech: “Interventions include the provision of water, sanitation and hygiene facilities, a child protection centre, nutrition screening items, recreational acce[ssories] and health supplies. We strive to ensure every child thrives.”

a2450.speaker: Dominic Mwandira, Nsanje District Commissioner
a2450.speech: Applauded the collaborative efforts in the response so far: “We are ma[k]ing a difference in the lives of these vulnerable children. Through collaborative efforts, the camp stands as a testament to resilience, community and the unwavering spirit of children.”

a2589.speaker: Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations
a2589.speech: pleaded in favour of the Sahel and Lake Chad regions before donors, calling for more support for the countries of the Sahel and the Lake Chad basin (Nigeria, Niger, Chad, Cameroon, Burkina Faso and Mali), and indicated that 33 million people currently need humanitarian aid and protection - including 11 million displaced people and refugees: "The United Nations is on the ground, helping governments and communities to provide food, health care, education and shelter. But we need more support. Our humanitarian response plans are funded at about 40%." ; He thanked contributors for their generosity while asking countries to redouble their efforts to fully fund the UN response plans.

a2589.speaker: Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations
a2589.speech: stressed that the Sahel and Lake Chad basin regions possess immense potential, with young and dynamic populations, as well as vast possibilities in the field of renewable energy, but that these regions face deep challenges, from violence and terrorism to the climate crisis, with floods that this year have upended the lives of some five million people.

a2589.speaker: Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations
a2589.speech: called for actions going beyond humanitarian aid, by tackling the root causes of the crises: reducing poverty and inequality, particularly for women and girls; adapting to climate change; promoting peace and democracy; and urging stakeholders to end hostilities, protect civilians and guarantee unimpeded humanitarian access: "The United Nations is eager to work with communities, countries, humanitarian partners, multilateral development banks and international funds to bring about change."

a2594.speaker: Dr. Salma Ibrahim Anas, Special Adviser to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Health Services, Federal Ministry of Health
a2594.speech: Hinted that the way to force down the cost of cancer diagnosis and treatment would be to initiate a campaign for a global fund, just as was done to mitigate the cost of treatment of HIV; said the exit of major pharmaceutical companies contributed to the high increase in the cost of diagnosis and treatment of cancer as 75 per cent of the drugs are imported into the country ; “We have good lessons that we can emulate... I must say it is very costly to be afflicted with cancer today, even if you are rich you will just move down the poverty line because of the high cost of diagnosis, high cost of treatment. But you know HIV was the same story... we told him Africans are not on treatment for HIV because of the high cost, and he said why?, are we second class citizens in the world? We must have Africans on treatment... And that was when we started the global fund. It was mobilized by President Obasanjo... We have more resources today including PEPFAR and the rest that provide treatment for people living with HIV... Let’s do it again, we have done it before, and I believe we can do it for cancer treatment.”

a2594.speaker: Dr. Salma Ibrahim Anas, Special Adviser to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Health Services, Federal Ministry of Health
a2594.speech: Disclosed that women are most affected by the disease, adding that there is a spike in cases among children and men, and harped on constant checks, stressing that some 50 per cent of cancer types can be easily prevented just by taking care of oneself.

a2594.speaker: Dr. Tunji Alausa, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a2594.speech: Disclosed that government will in a matter of weeks flag off construction of cancer control centers across all geo-political zones of the federation.

a2594.speaker: Dr. Tunji Alausa, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a2594.speech: “On the prevention of cervical cancer, on the 24 October 2023, as a country we introduced the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine into its routine immunization system, targeting 7.7 million girls, the largest number in a single round of HPV vaccination in the African region. The vaccine is being provided for free by the Federal Ministry of Health through the National Primary Health Care Development Agency with support from Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), World Health Organization (WHO) and other partners. Girls aged 9–14 years will receive a single dose of the vaccine, which is highly efficacious in preventing infection with HPV types 16 and 18 that are known to cause at least 70% of cervical cancers. Ladies and gentlemen, we know that reliable data indicate that, cervical cancer is the third most common cancer and the second most frequent cause of cancer deaths among women aged between 15 and 44 years. We have put in place campaigns in our schools and communities to increase the uptake of this vital single-dose vaccine. Again, we shall continue to encourage screening for cancer at all levels of our healthcare system.”

a2594.speaker: Runcie Chidebe, Convener of the event and Executive Director, Project PINK BLUE
a2594.speech: Said the symposium was part of his organization’s efforts to find solutions to easy cancer diagnosis and treatment; called for concerted efforts to decentralize facilities for diagnosis and treatment of the disease, lamenting the dearth of treatment centers across the country, a situation which he said makes early detection very difficult.

a2798.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communiqué)
a2798.speech: The Council of Ministers met in ordinary session on Wednesday 2 September 2015 and in extraordinary session on Thursday 3 September 2015 under the chairmanship of the President of the Republic, Head of State, Head of Government. At the beginning of the session, the Head of State observed a minute of silence in memory of the deceased (a list of named officials and relatives of officials).

a2798.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communiqué)
a2798.speech: Adopted several draft decrees, notably the draft decrees on the powers, organisation and functioning of the Prime Minister's Office, the ministry in charge of Microfinance, the Ministry of Youth Employment and Small and Medium Enterprises, the Ministry of Water, the Ministry of Industry and Commerce and the National Authority for State Action at Sea; a draft decree creating the National Council for Scientific and Technical Research (CNRST); draft decrees approving the creation of the “Anfani Communes Community” and the “Zou Communes Community” (CCZ); and a draft decree extending the transitional period for the effective establishment of the Agency for the Promotion of Investment and Exports (APIEX).

a2798.speaker: Minister of State in charge of the Economy, Finance and Denationalisation Programmes
a2798.speech: A communication relating to the project to revitalise the activities of the National Guarantee and Assistance Fund for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs).

a2798.speaker: Minister of State at the Presidency of the Republic in charge of the MDGs-SDGs and major works
a2798.speech: A communication reporting at mid-term on the formalities for the creation of the company Bénin-Tracteurs S.A. and on the financing offer of 250 million US dollars of Credit Suisse credit for the project to electrify 200 localities in Benin under the financial arrangement with the West African Development Bank (BOAD).

a2798.speaker: Minister in charge of the Economy
a2798.speech: An oral communication on the situation of SONACOP.

a2798.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (decision)
a2798.speech: In light of the information given by the minister and after discussion, the Council of Ministers decided to put in place a mechanism to monitor the functioning of SONACOP in order to strengthen its capacity to ensure supply to the stations and private groups. The mechanism comprises, in addition to the Director General of SONACOP, the Secretary General of the Presidency, the Auditor General and the President of the Energy Regulatory Authority. The Council of Ministers also instructed the Director General of SONACOP to present to it by next Wednesday communications on the projects submitted by national private partners.

a2798.speaker: Minister of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries
a2798.speech: A communication relating to Benin's participation in the 69th edition of the Chalon international fair, from 28 August to 7 September 2015.

a2798.speaker: Prime Minister in charge of Economic Development
a2798.speech: A communication reporting on the negotiation session relating to the Benin-Niger railway loop project, held from 4 to 6 April 2015 in Niamey between the delegation of the steering committee and the Bollé Group (Groupe Bolloré).

a2798.speaker: Minister of Public Works and Transport
a2798.speech: A communication reporting on the process of finalising the signature of the transfer agreements for the Benin-Niger rail link between the States of Benin and Niger and the Bolloré Group ; a communication from the same minister reporting on the development and asphalting works of the Djèrègbé-Dja-Owodé-Nigeria border road with regard to the clearing of the sites selected for the associated and reinforcement works.

a2798.speaker: Minister of Urban Planning, Housing and Sanitation
a2798.speech: A communication relating to the construction of two (02) new administrative towers in Cotonou as part of the implementation of the WAQF project. A mission will be carried out in Benin by the promoter of this administrative tower construction project within a fortnight for the start of the works.

a2798.speaker: Prime Minister of Benin
a2798.speech: An oral communication on a mission carried out in Paris in the framework of a programme called “Lumière pour tous” (Light for all), complementary to those under way, whose implementation will allow most households currently without it to have solar-powered lighting.

a2798.speaker: Minister of Energy, Petroleum and Mining Research and Development of Renewable Energies
a2798.speech: Two (02) communications relating to the signing of a concession agreement for the construction, ownership, operation and transfer of thermal power plants of 230 MW capacity with a start-up phase of 50 MW on the site of the SBEE Akpakpa power station in Cotonou by the company SATAREM ME, and to the sale of data acquired in the framework of the airborne geophysical campaign in partnership with the company CGG Service Inc.

a2798.speaker: Minister of the Interior, Public Security and Religious Affairs
a2798.speech: A communication on the radio-telecommunication equipment and accessories of the National Police.

a2798.speaker: Minister of National Defence
a2798.speech: Two communications reporting respectively on the administrative situation of civilian contract staff previously recruited for the Parakou Armed Forces Teaching Hospital, and on the operating subsidy to the Parakou Armed Forces Teaching Hospital.

a2798.speaker: Minister of Health
a2798.speech: Two communications relating to the report of the Commission responsible for verifying the management of the revenue of the Ouidah hospital for the 2014 financial year, and to the needs of the Borgou and Alibori Departmental University Teaching Hospital in the framework of its partnership with the Orléans Regional Hospital.

a2798.speaker: Minister of Communication and Information and Communication Technologies and Minister in charge of Youth Employment and Small and Medium Enterprises (joint communication)
a2798.speech: A joint communication relating to the continued operationalisation of the “Allô service public” service for users of the Beninese public administration and to the promotion of youth employment.

a2798.speaker: Minister in charge of Youth Employment and Small and Medium Enterprises
a2798.speech: A communication relating to the allocation of new resources for the project to set up Business Promotion Centres (BPC). From the examination of this communication, it emerges that the BPCs are arousing increasing interest among young job-seekers. Thus in 2014, close to sixty thousand (60,000) young people visited the BPCs already installed and operational. For 2015, by the end of June, forty-five thousand (45,000) had already visited these centres.

a2798.speaker: Minister of State in charge of the Economy, Finance and Denationalisation Programmes and Minister of Communication and Information and Communication Technologies (joint communication)
a2798.speech: A joint communication on the options for implementing the opening of the capital of Libercom SA, Bénin Télécom Services and Bénin Télécom Infrastructures SA.

a2798.speaker: Minister of Communication and Information and Communication Technologies
a2798.speech: A communication reporting on the pools of jobs that the digital economy holds. Taking note of this communication, the Council set up a committee composed of the Minister of State in charge of the Economy and the ministers in charge of Employment and of Information and Communication Technologies with a view to examining the question in greater depth for the creation of new jobs in this sector.

a2798.speaker: Minister of Decentralisation, Local Governance, Administration and Territorial Planning
a2798.speech: A report on the audit mission of the management of the resources of the Fund for Support to the Development of Communes (FADeC) transferred to the communes in 2013.

a2798.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (authorisations)
a2798.speech: The Council of Ministers authorised the participation of the Head of State in the signing ceremony of the 2nd Millennium Challenge Account Benin Compact in Washington, DC from 7 to 13 September 2015 and in the United Nations summit devoted to the adoption of the post-2015 development agenda and the general debate of the seventieth session of the General Assembly in New York from 25 to 27 September 2015; the official visits to Benin of His Excellency Theodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, President of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea, and of His Excellency Mr Jacob Zuma, President of the Republic of South Africa; the organisation of the Hadj 2015; the swearing-in ceremony of the Young Volunteers of Professional Expertise for 2015; a reflection seminar on the transition to Digital Terrestrial Television in Cotonou on 24 and 25 September 2015; reflection days on the participation of the Beninese Armed Forces in local development tasks; the entrance examination to Form 6 at the Bembéréké Military Prytaneum and the Natitingou Girls' Military High School for the 2015-2016 academic year; the mission to evaluate national capacities for disaster risk reduction and emergency response preparedness in Benin from 7 to 19 September 2015; and the statutory meetings for 2015 of the Ministry of Justice, Legislation and Human Rights and of the Ministry of the Maritime Economy and Port Infrastructure.

a2798.speaker: Alassani Tigri, Secretary General of the Government of Benin (official communiqué)
a2798.speech: Issued the communiqué announcing the appointments made: at the Presidency of the Republic, on the proposal of the President of the Republic — Colonel Abou ISSA as President of the National Commission for the Fight against the Proliferation of Small Arms (CNLCPAL), cumulatively with his current functions; Captain (Colonel) Maxime Ahoyo as Maritime Prefect; Lieutenant-Colonel Saturnin Obelakou as Head of the Land Division of the President's military cabinet; Squadron Leader Firmin Boko as Head of the Gendarmerie/Police Division; Commander Hervé Alotchénou as Head of the Air Division; Colonel Tchankpega Sansiman as Head of the Transmission Security Service of the Presidency; Mr Karimou Morou as Technical Adviser on Food and Nutritional Security; and Mr Vinakpo Aristide Alovokpinhoun as Technical Adviser on the Promotion of Youth Employment. At the Ministry of Communication and ICT, on the proposal of the Minister: Mrs Jémila Claire Sossouhounto, wife Bassabi Djara, as Secretary General of the ministry. At the Ministry of Labour, the Civil Service and Administrative and Institutional Reform, on the proposal of the Minister and after the concurring opinion of the Board of Directors of the National Social Security Fund: Mr Martial Sounton as Director General of the National Social Security Fund. Remise à disposition: Mr Appolinaire Houénou, returned to the disposal of the Ministry of State in charge of the Economy, Finance and Denationalisation Programmes. Done at Cotonou, 2 September 2015.

a2802.speaker: DP World
a2802.speech: is now claiming one billion dollars before the London Court of Arbitration, exposing Djibouti to heavy financial penalties.

a2802.speaker: Container Port Performance Index (2022-2023)
a2802.speech: ranked the port of Djibouti as having fallen from 26th to 379th place worldwide.

a2802.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2802.speech: According to the IMF, the Chinese loans caused public debt to double, reaching a worrying 104% of GDP in 2019.

a2802.speaker: Aboubaker Hadi, head of the Djibouti Ports and Free Zones Authority (DPFZA) and Great Horn Investment Holding (GHIH)
a2802.speech: made accusations of clientelism against Djama Ibrahim Darar in 2025, which had the sole purpose of strengthening his own grip on power.

a2802.speaker: Panama Papers (2015)
a2802.speech: documented Hadi's involvement, which seriously tarnished his international reputation.

a2810.speaker: A number of economic analysts
a2810.speech: suggest it's the Middle East that can most help the world's struggling economies, but only once the region takes on a long overdue leadership role in the global economy's financial regulatory and development bodies. They stressed that there is considerable room for improvement in the leadership of the global economic system, which remains marked by the hubris of over-consumption especially by Western economies, unfair globalization, and under regulation of major banks ; specifically call on the leaders of the prosperous Middle East countries to play an immediate role now, and an ongoing role hereafter, in the world's leading regulatory and development bodies. They believe there are two imperatives: first, personal consumption in all countries must be much more in balance with internal consumer goods production; second, the major "surplus nations" need to immediately deploy a significant portion of their accumulated foreign reserves to where it will do the most good in stimulating weak parts of the world economy, whether within their own economies, overseas in the form of long-term development loans, and/or in Official Development Assistance (ODA).

a2810.speaker: World Bank data
a2810.speech: recent World Bank data revealed that the personal expenditures of Americans account for about 68 percent of the nation's GDP, which is up to 10 percentage points higher than in most other developed countries and a full 30 points higher than in China.

a2810.speaker: Abbas Zuaiter, Co-managing member and CIO of Zuaiter Capital Holdings
a2810.speech: stated that as further backdrop to what needs to be done now, it's important to reflect on the significant changes brought about by the global financial crisis a decade ago and the subsequent challenges of immigration, starting with changes in political and social stability: political and social stability are now clearly at risk across the globe, within Europe, in several of the former Russian satellites, in Latin America, and in Africa, where the continent's once combined, albeit modest, current account surplus has declined into a deficit and food security is in a perilous state. According to Abbas Zuaiter, over and above Brexit, there will likely be a further reordering of the European Union, and there will be perhaps as many as 30 failed states among the 60 or so small constitutional democracies which formed in the last half century, along with a rise in ethnic or state-sponsored nationalism.

a2810.speaker: Abbas Zuaiter, Co-managing member and CIO of Zuaiter Capital Holdings
a2810.speech: stressed that there are several steps the region needs to take to achieve its potential, but the goal is achievable: the Middle East needs, as Singapore once did, to embrace a master economic plan which facilitates private sector enterprise; instead of the region's governments being the allocators of capital, these governments need to get out of the way and allow private sector entrepreneurs to fairly earn their cost of capital; the rule of law needs to be implemented and enforced across the board, open free trade must be allowed, foreign property rights must be respected, the religious rights of all citizens must be protected, and the region's massive sovereign wealth funds must either lend to or at least be used to provide first-loss protection to private sector enterprises.

a2810.speaker: Leo Hindery Jr., Chairman and CEO of Trine Acquisition Corp
a2810.speech: stated that the prosperous Middle East governments must also seek out major roles within the World Bank and the IMF, within the ongoing reform efforts aimed at the major banks and investment houses, and within responsible non-discriminatory Official Development Assistance initiatives, especially throughout the Islamic world and in Africa; initially, these new external roles may be hard for some of the region's nations to accept for cultural, bureaucratic, and political reasons.

a2810.speaker: Leo Hindery Jr., Chairman and CEO of Trine Acquisition Corp
a2810.speech: noted that it's also past time for there to be free trade agreements in place among all the Arab countries, and with the strong encouragement of the United States there needs to be a Middle East equivalent of the European Monetary Union. Fifteen Middle East countries ranging from Algeria to Yemen are short of capital and long on unemployed people, while countries like Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE are long on capital and short on people.

a2905.speaker: Vulnerability Assessment and Analysis Report for 2023-2024
a2905.speech: Indicates that 172,000 households are expected to face high levels of acute food insecurity between March 2023 and June 2024.

a2905.speaker: Namibian Cabinet
a2905.speech: Authorised the Office of the Prime Minister to consider a revision of the commencement date of the livestock drought programme to 1 July, subject to an assessment of the number of affected farmers and their financial implications.

a3132.speaker: Jim Wright, USAID/Liberia Mission Director
a3132.speech: has congratulated Rachelle Kanneh for winning Liberia’s Young Journalist Award 2024; commended the award winner for her incredible achievements; also encouraged her to continue highlighting the issues affecting women and girls through her stories and radio programs; reiterated the mission’s commitment to supporting Liberia’s media development at all levels.

a3132.speaker: Lien Bach, Internews Chief of Party
a3132.speech: thanked USAID Liberia and the United States government for their continuous support towards media development in Liberia; said the Liberia Media Activity project is aimed at enhancing media development across the different stages ranging from grassroots to top levels; emphasized that despite the challenges, Internews Liberia has made significant strides in improving media content and strengthening capacity development.

a3132.speaker: Varmah Kamara, Executive Director of Youth Media Action (YMA)
a3132.speech: lauded USAID Liberia and Internews Liberia for their support over the years; added that the Young Journalist Award is an opportunity for young Liberian journalists to showcase their media talents, something he believes has been lacking in the past; believes that the program has seen significant improvement in young reporters' media content, especially for entry-level reporters in rural communities.

a3132.speaker: Rachelle Kanneh, award winner / Young Journalist Award 2024 recipient
a3132.speech: thanked USAID Liberia for the support through Internews in Liberia and Youth Media Action while she promised to serve as an ambassador in promoting girls' and women’s rights in Gbarpolu County.

a3209.speaker: Sir Ken Robinson
a3209.speech: “Universities are designed in their own image. They reward a certain type of intelligence and a certain type of talent, which happens to be academic.”

a3227.speaker: Boniface Jacob ('Boni Yai'), Chairman of Chadema's Coast Zone and former mayor of Ubungo
a3227.speech: Described his unique journey to winning the position while in prison, after being arrested and charged with cybercrime offences; recounted the challenges and difficult decisions he made to allow Chadema's Coast Zone to proceed with the election, which he had initially wanted postponed until the outcome of his bail was known; said his arrest involved some scuffling between him and the police and caused a commotion among passers-by and customers at the restaurant; said that because the course of his case was unclear, he initially sent his lawyers to ask the party to postpone the election scheduled for September 28; said the party agreed and postponed it, but after seeing his bail delayed and after advice he received in remand he decided otherwise: "And there in prison the convicts and remand prisoners advised me to ask the party to go ahead with the election process, otherwise I would not get out. The thinking of prison people - they told me that if I insisted on my position that the election should not take place, I would stay in prison for a long time; instead they advised me to let the process continue, regardless of whether I won or not."

a3227.speaker: Boniface Jacob ('Boni Yai'), Chairman of Chadema's Coast Zone
a3227.speech: Said that despite hopes of victory due to his preparations, on election day, Saturday October 5, he was anxious because he was in prison: "While the election was taking place I did not get the results in time; I expected to know by midday, but I became anxious because under prison procedures from 3 p.m. we are required to go to sleep. By that time I was going to the sleeping area without any news at all about the results, and until 9 p.m. when I slept I knew nothing" ; said the following morning he went to watch television but did not manage to see newspaper headlines; said remand prisoners and convicts came to him cheering and calling him "chairman, chairman": "They lifted me up high; I asked them, by how many votes did I win? They did not know, other than to say I had won by 77 percent. They told me that I and my whole team had won; they congratulated me a lot."

a3227.speaker: Boniface Jacob ('Boni Yai'), Chairman of Chadema's Coast Zone
a3227.speech: Said he had no doubt about winning because of his preparations starting from taking out and returning the forms: "My numbers (voters) were good from the time I returned the forms; they backed me by a large percentage. Another thing is that the Coast has for a long time lacked an energising person who, when he stands up, you really say Chadema has stood up. But another thing, I knew the problem of the Coast people, that they wanted lively leadership, not a sluggish one" ; said another thing that carried him was his history of successful struggles: "The candidate was inside (remand) but his qualities were outside. Fortunately my history carried me: Boniface is a fighter, a leader, I have been on the central committee at different times. On the day of returning the forms I told them what I want the Coast Zone to be, so I was not surprised to be told I had won, although I received the results while sitting on a bench in prison" ; praised the major improvements made in prison, including cleanliness and the presence of a television.

a3227.speaker: Boniface Jacob ('Boni Yai'), Chairman of Chadema's Coast Zone
a3227.speech: Said that activism defending human rights using social media platforms is not easy because he deals with people directly, so his lifestyle must change: "There is nothing that has no consequences; first, my way of life has changed because of this activism of being on the front line fighting for human rights. My security arrangement has changed; right now there are some areas I cannot visit. Also, I cannot sit in a bar or entertainment places until dawn as I used to before the incidents of people disappearing and being abducted returned. In the past I could stay up until morning, but now I cannot, it is not safe for me" ; said there are people of good will who may seek him out for help, but in the life of activism it is not easy for him to meet everyone: "I have changed my eating pattern; I cannot eat everywhere or walk in every area, even during the day, because I am seen as a threat to people who do improper things in society" ; said the environment of his businesses has changed and he has left management to others: "I have also incurred losses; every three months I must buy a new phone because when I am arrested I leave them with the police. Right now I have four phones held by the Police Force. Also, the lawyers handling my cases I pay them, it is not free, this is also a loss."

a3227.speaker: Boniface Jacob ('Boni Yai'), Chairman of Chadema's Coast Zone
a3227.speech: Asked about his strategies in the new position, said that in Bagamoyo, Chalinze, Mafia, Kibaha Urban and Rural there is great enthusiasm, as in the Dar es Salaam constituencies; said the big problem of the Coast Region is the poor economic situation and the lack of civic education that would make citizens believe there are alternative parties: "The operations that took place there in Kibiti, Rufiji and Mkuranga instilled fear in people about carrying out political activities, something that frightened the residents of those areas" ; said that to strengthen the party he will provide civic education to the people of Kibiti, Mkuranga and Rufiji so they can have confidence to take part in political activities: "In my leadership I will ensure citizens return to a normal state of life; I will hold many meetings and sessions to give them courage and morale. There are people capable of contesting for leadership in those areas, but they fear for their safety, that if they are seen opposing CCM they will be in a difficult situation" ; said he will ensure senior party leaders including Chadema Chairman Freeman Mbowe, Vice Chairman-Mainland Tundu Lissu and central committee members go to those areas to hold public rallies regularly.

a3227.speaker: Fellow remand prisoners and convicts at Segerea Prison
a3227.speech: Advised him to ask the party to go ahead with the election process, otherwise he would not get out; informed him of his victory, telling him he had won by 77 percent and that he and his whole team had won.

a3279.speaker: Al-Shabaab
a3279.speech: Ever since October 2011, when 4,000-odd Kenyan troops were dispatched across the border into Somalia with a mandate to hunt down and destroy Al-Shabaab, the Islamist militant group has been promising a massive, bloody revenge.

a3279.speaker: Analysts
a3279.speech: Said at the time that the Mumbai 2008 attacks could be the template for terrorism of the future.

a3279.speaker: William Ruto, Deputy President of Kenya
a3279.speech: Has requested that the International Criminal Court delay his trial so that he can deal with the aftermath of the massacre.

a3378.speaker: Government of Liberia
a3378.speech: Has announced a breakthrough in reviving its partnership with the U.S. Government’s Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC), marking a significant milestone in the country’s development agenda, and that Liberia has now been officially proposed for reaffirmation into the MCC Compact program.

a3378.speaker: Alicia Robinson-Morgan, Managing Director for Africa at the MCC (formal communication/letter)
a3378.speech: Confirmed in formal communication to Liberia that Liberia is under active review by the Board for potential reaffirmation, and that the MCC Board of Directors is expected to convene next week to deliberate on Liberia’s eligibility and possible readmittance into the Compact formulation process.

a3378.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberia’s Finance and Development Planning Minister
a3378.speech: Termed Liberia’s selection into the MCC multi-million-dollar program as a major milestone for the government: “We’ve received a strong signal from Washington. Ms. Robinson-Morgan’s letter informs us that Liberia’s name has been put forward for reaffirmation, and the MCC Board will be meeting next week to consider our final approval. All indicators are pointing in the right direction.” ; “This is where we are today. We’ve moved from pause to play. The MCC Board’s proposed reaffirmation is a strong vote of confidence in Liberia’s direction. While the final decision is still ahead, we are confident, we are on track, and we are ready to deliver for the Liberian people.”

a3378.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberia’s Finance and Development Planning Minister
a3378.speech: Emphasized that this progress is the result of deliberate and strategic diplomacy by President Joseph Nyuma Boakai and his team: “The President was not just speaking good English in Washington during the U.S.-Africa Leaders’ Summit—he was making impactful moves on multiple fronts. His recent visit to the United States has clearly played a major role in reigniting this process.”
