a3378.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberia’s Finance and Development Planning Minister
a3378.speech: Said the new Compact could bring in funding exceeding US$500 million, or slightly less depending on the outcome of final negotiations, supporting critical national development priorities including infrastructure, economic growth, governance reforms, and education.

a3514.speaker: Ministry of International Relations and Trade (MIRT), Namibia
a3514.speech: Has reiterated its resolve to strengthen economic diplomacy and ensure small and medium enterprises' access to external markets.

a3514.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, President of Namibia
a3514.speech: Says Namibia's foreign policy is increasingly shaped by the imperative of economic diplomacy; she says this is no longer a complementary aspect of international engagement but a central instrument in advancing national development objectives ; has emphasised that merging the trade function with international relations was a deliberate move to ensure Namibia fully leverages economic diplomacy through its foreign policy.

a3514.speaker: Zhao Weiping, Chinese Ambassador to Namibia
a3514.speech: Has said tariffs imposed on them by the United States would only have a positive impact on ties between China and Namibia ; said the increase in tariffs by the US was a typical act of economic bullying by America.

a3514.speaker: Some members of Namibia's National Assembly
a3514.speech: Have commended the Ministry of International Relations and Trade for its active internship programme and urged the ministry to expand efforts to promote job opportunities for Namibians abroad.

a3514.speaker: Governments of Namibia and Angola (farewell courtesy meeting between President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah and Angola's Ambassador Jovelina Imperial e Costa)
a3514.speech: Remain committed to realising the objectives of economic diplomacy.

a3514.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
a3514.speech: Has encouraged the new Heads of Mission to find niche markets for Namibia's products and said they are also expected to assist with the improvement of the country's global competitiveness rankings, as he commissioned three Heads of Mission at State House.

a3514.speaker: Hage Geingob, President of Namibia
a3514.speech: Commended the outgoing High Commissioner, Dr. Modestus Kipilimba, for actively promoting cooperation in this regard, the sound bilateral ties between Namibia and Tanzania having entered the stage of economic diplomacy ; urged the new Heads of Mission to promote bilateral ties premised on economic diplomacy to benefit their respective countries and Namibia.

a4001.speaker: Ana Lima, housewife and mother of three (consumer at the Assomada market)
a4001.speech: Told A NAÇÃO: “Now I can do the shopping for the whole week without going over budget” ; “Money no longer goes as far as it used to, so this drop in prices helps a lot.”

a4001.speaker: Dona Júlia, vegetable seller at the Assomada market for more than 20 years
a4001.speech: Laments: “There are days when we have to throw away half of what we brought because we have nowhere to keep it. We lose a lot.”

a4001.speaker: Vendors and consumers at the Assomada market
a4001.speech: Call for concrete action from local and national authorities, demanding the rehabilitation of the market’s infrastructure, the creation of refrigeration systems, and the development of distribution channels that avoid losses and give value to the work of small producers and traders.

a4081.speaker: Gloria Ogbaki, Head of Information and Public Relations, National Biosafety Management Agency (NBMA)
a4081.speech: In a statement released on Monday, emphasised that all GM products in Nigeria undergo a rigorous, science-based approval process conducted by the agency. "We wish to reassure Nigerians that no GMO enters or is used in Nigeria without passing through the Agency's strict, science-based approval process."

a4081.speaker: National Biosafety Management Agency (NBMA) (press statement)
a4081.speech: Reaffirmed its dedication to ensuring the safe utilisation of Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs) in Nigeria, and warned that any importer or producer found to contravene the NBMA Act 2015 (as amended) will face appropriate sanctions, as the Agency will not hesitate to enforce the law to protect Nigerians, the environment, and biodiversity. "Our responsibility is clear: to protect human health, biodiversity, and the environment while ensuring Nigerians have access to safe innovation."

a4081.speaker: National Biosafety Management Agency (NBMA) (press statement)
a4081.speech: Explained that before any genetically modified organism can be imported, produced, or commercialised in Nigeria, it undertakes a rigorous screening and requires a detailed application supported by scientific data, risk assessments, and safety studies; said it publishes each application in at least two national newspapers and deposits copies at strategic locations across the country, with a 21-day public notice allowing Nigerians and stakeholders to review the application, raise concerns, or provide feedback. "Independent experts are then brought into the process. A National Biosafety Committee and a Technical Sub-Committee, made up of relevant scientists from universities, research institutes, professional bodies, and government agencies, carefully review the evidence." ; "Decisions are made strictly on science. Only GMOs proven to be as safe as their conventional counterparts are approved; those that present risks are rejected outright."

a4081.speaker: National Biosafety Management Agency (NBMA) (press statement)
a4081.speech: Reiterated that its monitoring does not stop after GM approval, because its officers carry out regular post-release monitoring and inspection to ensure full compliance. "We also carry out quarterly surveillance and any breach attracts tough sanctions, including seizure, destruction, or repatriation of unauthorised GMOs. And as the Agency has warned, any importer or producer who violates the NBMA Act will face firm sanctions without hesitation."

a4081.speaker: Gloria Ogbaki, Head of Information and Public Relations, National Biosafety Management Agency (NBMA)
a4081.speech: "Science, not sentiment, guides our decisions", because the NBMA aligns its processes with global best practices, including standards of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), the Codex Alimentarius Commission, and the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety ; "Consumer rights are protected," noting that labelling of GMOs is mandatory by law, to safeguard Nigerians' freedom of choice.

a4081.speaker: National Biosafety Management Agency (NBMA) (press statement)
a4081.speech: "Nigeria is a continental leader. Our regulatory system has been recognised across Africa and has served as a model for several countries building their biosafety frameworks." ; "Our duty is to protect Nigerians without stifling innovation, and we will continue to discharge this mandate with transparency, firmness, and scientific integrity." ; Urged the public and stakeholders to place trust in Nigeria's biosafety system.

a4081.speaker: PREMIUM TIMES investigation in collaboration with Lighthouse Reports and other media partners
a4081.speech: Unveiled that the NBMA has been operating under the influence of the now-defunct United States Agency for International Development (USAID); this influence has facilitated the approval of GMO crops while minimising the perceived risks associated with pesticide usage in Nigeria.

a4081.speaker: PREMIUM TIMES investigation (2022)
a4081.speech: Revealed that across several communities in Nigeria, farmers growing GM crop varieties know too little to make informed decisions.

a4095.speaker: Bill Gates, co-chair of the Gates Foundation
a4095.speech: “I recently made a commitment that my wealth will be given away over the next 20 years. The majority of that funding will be spent on helping you address challenges here in Africa.” ; “By unleashing human potential through health and education, every country in Africa should be on a path to prosperity – and that path is an exciting thing to be part of.” ; underscored the critical role of African leadership and ingenuity in driving the continent’s health and economic future.

a4095.speaker: Bill Gates, co-chair of the Gates Foundation
a4095.speech: Called for prioritizing primary healthcare, emphasizing that “investing in primary healthcare has the greatest impact on health and wellbeing.” ; “With primary healthcare, what we’ve learned is that helping the mother be healthy and have great nutrition before she gets pregnant, while she is pregnant, delivers the strongest results. Ensuring the child receives good nutrition in their first four years as well makes all the difference.”

a4095.speaker: Bill Gates, co-chair of the Gates Foundation
a4095.speech: Reflecting on more than two decades of engagement on the continent: “I’ve always been inspired by the hard work of Africans even in places with very limited resources.” ; “The kind of field work to get solutions out, even in the most rural areas, has been incredible.”

a4095.speaker: Bill Gates, co-chair of the Gates Foundation
a4095.speech: Spoke about the transformative potential of artificial intelligence, praising Africa’s young innovators: “seeing young people in Africa embracing this, and thinking about how it applies to the problems that they want to solve.” ; “Africa largely skipped traditional banking and now you have a chance, as you build your next generation healthcare systems, to think about how AI is built into that.” ; “Rwanda is using AI to improve service delivery. E.g. AI-enabled ultrasound, to identify high-risk pregnancies earlier, helping women receive timely, potentially life-saving care.”

a4095.speaker: Bill Gates, co-chair of the Gates Foundation
a4095.speech: “Our foundation has an increasing commitment to Africa. Our first African office was here in Ethiopia about 13 years ago. Now we have offices in South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria and Senegal. That’s a great way for us to strengthen partnerships.”

a4095.speaker: Graça Machel, advocate for women and children
a4095.speech: Described the current situation as “a moment of crisis” and emphasized the importance of enduring partnerships in Africa’s development journey: “Mr Gates’ long-standing partnership with Africa reflects a deep understanding of these challenges and a respect for African leadership, ideas and innovation. We are counting on Mr Gates’ steadfast commitment to continue walking this path of transformation alongside us.”

a4095.speaker: Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, Director-General of the World Trade Organization
a4095.speech: Emphasized that Africa’s health progress is a result of strong government leadership, resilient communities, and partnerships that deliver results.

a4095.speaker: Prominent African leaders, including Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (WTO Director-General) and Amina J. Mohammed (UN Deputy Secretary-General)
a4095.speech: Delivered calls for collaboration and shared responsibility.

a4246.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (inaugural address)
a4246.speech: President Trump's inaugural address focused on trade tariffs, energy deregulation, immigration policies, and a reprieve for TikTok, with no mention of cryptocurrencies.

a4246.speaker: Geoffrey Kendrick, Global Head of Digital Assets Research at Standard Chartered (via Reuters report)
a4246.speech: “The digital asset market is disappointed to not have been mentioned in the inauguration speech or day-one executive orders. I suspect Bitcoin will go lower in the absence of news from Trump on digital assets. A break below $100,000 seems inevitable.”

a4246.speaker: CoinMarketCap (data)
a4246.speech: According to data from CoinMarketCap, the Trump-branded token, initially priced at $6.50 at its Friday night launch and peaking at $75 on Monday, has since halved in value to $37.98.

a4248.speaker: Rui Semedo, President of the PAICV party (Cabo Verde)
a4248.speech: At a press conference in Praia, recommended that the country organise itself to respond to the mass deportation of undocumented Cape Verdeans from the United States, by creating the conditions for deportees to receive the necessary support, such as access to mechanisms allowing them to be covered by lawyers and to defend legality and their rights; stressed that the country must inform itself better about the situation, make the necessary contacts with the American authorities and set up an organisation for the reception, welcoming, follow-up and support of these immigrants ; “It is a matter of extended deportation that requires special care, even if the Government has previously taken care to receive deportees; at this moment there will have to be special concerns because it is a new situation,” reiterating the need to know the scale and number of those threatened with expulsion.

a4248.speaker: Rui Semedo, President of the PAICV party (Cabo Verde)
a4248.speech: On the suspension of United States foreign aid, specifically the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) package, said he hoped negotiations would be resumed and that Cabo Verde would not be removed from the list of beneficiaries of the cooperation ; “As a party we express the wish that the issue be restored and that Cabo Verde benefit from this important financing,” adding that the Government should use every means of influence and negotiation to continue to have access to this source of financing.

a4248.speaker: United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement
a4248.speech: According to the service, on Thursday the 23rd a total of 538 foreigners were arrested and 373 were placed in detention in the first actions following Trump's decree.

a4248.speaker: United States Department of Homeland Security (data)
a4248.speech: According to its data, Trump's goal of accelerating deportations to one million per year is considered double the maximum number of deportations carried out in a single year in recent decades.

a4307.speaker: Lakhdar Brahimi, international mediator of the Syrian crisis
a4307.speech: Managed to bring the government and opposition delegations together around the same table in order to remind them of the fundamentals of Geneva 2.

a4307.speaker: Syrian rebel coalition (opposition)
a4307.speech: Demands a transitional government in which Bashar al-Assad would have no role to play.

a4307.speaker: Damascus / Assad government side
a4307.speech: Retorts “Out of the question” to the demand that Assad have no role in a transitional government.

a4475.speaker: Barack Obama, President of the United States
a4475.speech: Announced from Poland that his administration is committing to release – subject to the approval of Congress – the sum of one billion dollars to contribute to the security of the countries of Eastern Europe, to be used to deploy new land, air and naval forces in Eastern Europe and to finance the sending of American experts to install equipment improving existing military infrastructure in the zone.

a4518.speaker: Some formal humanitarian actors
a4518.speech: Question diaspora actors' impartiality when they assist areas of origin.

a4518.speaker: Diaspora humanitarian actors
a4518.speech: Criticise the international system for not taking local realities into consideration and for being slow and bureaucratic, as well as for having disproportionate administration costs and control.

a4518.speaker: Mohamed Aden Hassan & Nauja Kleist (policy brief authors)
a4518.speech: Based on policy dialogues and interviews with humanitarian actors and experts in Hargeisa and Nairobi, the policy brief explores ideal modes of collaboration that connect the strengths of each system without merging them, and suggests ways forward while acknowledging dilemmas and challenges; argues that it is crucial for international agencies to engage in dialogues with affected communities and understand local provisions of support and aid already in place, and that if localisation is to be more than an abstract ideal, the international humanitarian system must increase its local engagement as a key element in providing practical, respectful and sustainable aid, since in a situation where humanitarian needs are growing while funds are dwindling, dialogue and mutual learning is more important than ever.

a4569.speaker: AU Peace and Security Council (Heads of State and Government meeting)
a4569.speech: Unanimously endorsed the Moroccan proposal to observe a humanitarian truce in Sudan during the holy month of Ramadan, in order to allow access for humanitarian aid without restriction or discrimination.

a4569.speaker: Morocco (at the AU high-level meeting on health financing)
a4569.speech: Announced a substantial contribution with the aim of strengthening health security within the continent.

a4605.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a4605.speech: Said on Wednesday that he was aiming for a meeting on Friday in Washington with Donald Trump to finalise a framework agreement on the exploitation of Ukrainian minerals; “There is a working date [...] Friday” for the trip to Washington ; assured that the sticking points – in particular over the sum of 500 billion dollars of American aid mentioned by Mr Trump – had finally disappeared.

a4605.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a4605.speech: Said he wanted to ask his American counterpart whether he really intended to “halt” assistance to Ukraine: “My question will be very direct: are the United States going to stop support or not? Will we be able to buy weapons (from the United States), if it is no longer aid?”

a4605.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a4605.speech: Had rejected the earlier agreement, refusing to sign a text that “ten generations of Ukrainians” would have to pay for; raised the possibility of an exchange of mineral wealth for security guarantees as early as October, when he presented the broad lines of his “victory plan”.

a4605.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4605.speech: Called Volodymyr Zelensky a “dictator” and took up the Kremlin's talking points on the causes of the Russian invasion since February 2022; said he absolutely wanted the agreement as compensation for the military and financial aid provided over the past three years, hammering home that he wanted compensation.

a4605.speaker: Sergei Lavrov, Russian Foreign Minister
a4605.speech: Said that diplomats from Russia and the United States would meet on Thursday in Istanbul as the two countries continue discussions with a view to overhauling their bilateral relations.

a4605.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President, and Keir Starmer, British Prime Minister
a4605.speech: Are seeking to convince Donald Trump that an overall agreement for “a lasting peace” in Ukraine can only be found with their participation and that of the Ukrainian authorities.

a4605.speaker: Giorgia Meloni, Italian Prime Minister
a4605.speech: Demanded on Wednesday that “security guarantees” be given to Kyiv “within the framework of NATO” in order to reach a “just” peace.

a4605.speaker: Ukrainian authorities
a4605.speech: Reported that Russian bombardment of Ukraine's towns and villages on Wednesday caused at least seven deaths, including five in the Donetsk region and a Ukrainian journalist of the state news agency Ukrinform, Tetiana Koulyk.

a4605.speaker: Ukrinform (Ukrainian state news agency)
a4605.speech: Reported that Tetiana Koulyk's house in the Bucha district, near Kyiv, was hit by a Russian drone during the night from Tuesday to Wednesday, and that another body was found at the site.

a4605.speaker: Ukrainian army
a4605.speech: Claimed a successful counter-offensive near Pokrovsk, a town in eastern Ukraine that Russian troops are trying to conquer, and in the vicinity of a key motorway serving the large city of Dnipro.

a4605.speaker: Kiel Institute for the World Economy (IfW Kiel)
a4605.speech: Cited for the figure that assistance provided to Ukraine so far amounts to some 120 billion dollars, roughly a quarter of the 500 billion dollar commitment Washington envisaged.

a4605.speaker: Senior Ukrainian official / Ukrainian source informed of the content of the compromise (anonymous, interviewed by AFP)
a4605.speech: Said the American financial claim is no longer in the document; that the Americans agreed to remove “all the clauses that did not suit us, in particular the 500 billion dollars”; that discussions are still under way on the security point; and explained, “It is a general clause which says that America will invest in a sovereign, stable and prosperous Ukraine, that it is working for a lasting peace and that America supports efforts towards security guarantees.”

a4605.speaker: World Mining Data
a4605.speech: Cited as the source for Ukraine's ranking as the 8th largest world producer of manganese, 11th of titanium and 14th of graphite.

a4605.speaker: French Bureau of Geological and Mining Research (BRGM)
a4605.speech: Notes that Ukraine concentrates “20% of estimated world resources” of graphite and is “one of the main countries in Europe in terms of potential” for lithium exploitation.

a4605.speaker: Ukrainian government
a4605.speech: Maintains that Ukraine has on its territory “one of the vastest resources” of lithium in Europe, but that it is not extracted “to date”; admits that developing the Novopoltavske deposit in the Zaporizhzhia region would on its own require 300 million dollars of investment.

a4605.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President / the Kremlin
a4605.speech: The Kremlin has ruled out ceding the zones under its control; Vladimir Putin has said he is favourable to American investment in these occupied regions.

a4605.speaker: ledevoir.com
a4605.speech: Cited as the source of the article.

a4648.speaker: Alpha S. Diallo, Deputy USAID Representative in Djibouti
a4648.speech: began by thanking the Minister for the friendly welcome extended to the delegation, before explaining the purpose of the meeting, which was the presentation of a project entitled “Citizen Engagement, Advocacy and Accountability,” worth 10 million US dollars and financed through a USAID envelope; he explained that the project aims to better equip civil society organizations in the interior regions by strengthening their legal status and supporting them toward more responsive local governance, with citizen engagement as the ultimate objective ; “The main objective of the project is the strengthening of citizen participation and advocacy for more responsive local governance.”

a4648.speaker: Kassim Haroun Ali, Minister of Decentralization of Djibouti
a4648.speech: thanked the USAID team for their visit and recalled that his department is cross-cutting, dealing with the sectoral ministries on all subjects relating to regional development, and gave assurances that his department is available and willing to make every effort for the implementation of this project ; “The role of the Ministry Delegate in charge of decentralization is to bring the administration closer to those it serves, to contribute to inclusive development by carrying out the implementation of the decentralization process as desired by the President of the Republic, Mr. Ismail Omar Guelleh, and as charted by my department’s roadmap” ; “In this sense, my department is prepared to contribute substantially by acting as a focal point to facilitate the implementation and the smooth running of the said project.”

a4716.speaker: World Malaria Report 2024
a4716.speech: According to the report, Nigeria is responsible for a staggering 31 percent of global malaria deaths and 27 percent of total cases worldwide.

a4716.speaker: Dr. Iziaq Adekunle Salako, Honourable Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a4716.speech: Revealed the statistic on Friday at the 2025 World Malaria Day commemoration in Abuja and emphasised that malaria remains one of Nigeria's most pressing public health challenges, especially affecting children under five and pregnant women: "This disease not only causes suffering and death, but it also disrupts the economic ecosystem by hindering productivity and increasing healthcare costs."

a4716.speaker: Dr. Iziaq Adekunle Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a4716.speech: Attributed the country's intensified fight against malaria to the high-level political support from President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, noting that malaria elimination is top on the health agenda of the current administration.

a4716.speaker: Dr. Iziaq Adekunle Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a4716.speech: Highlighted several federal government interventions, including the Rethinking Malaria Initiative and the establishment of the Advisory on Malaria Elimination in Nigeria (AMEN), and said these efforts are already driving change; said the federal government plans to distribute insecticide-treated mosquito nets across 12 states, that over 30 million children under five in the northern region will benefit from Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention (SMC), announced the first-ever pilot of Larval Source Management in six states, and said the phased rollout of the malaria vaccine which began in December 2024 in Kebbi and Bayelsa will expand to 17 more states this year.

a4716.speaker: Dr. Iziaq Adekunle Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a4716.speech: In response to the U.S. 'Stop Work Order' affecting malaria activities by USAID/PMI, assured Nigerians that the federal government has made budgetary provisions to bridge the funding gap and will procure life-saving commodities such as ACTs, RDT kits, injectable artesunate, and preventive drugs for pregnant women.

a4716.speaker: Dr. Iziaq Adekunle Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a4716.speech: Announced two major surveys - the Rapid Impact Assessment and the Malaria Indicator Survey - to monitor the effectiveness of interventions and track disease prevalence nationwide.

a4716.speaker: Dr. Iziaq Adekunle Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a4716.speech: Acknowledged the critical role of partners including WHO, UNICEF, Global Fund, and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, and commended the Nigeria End Malaria Council chaired by business magnate Alhaji Aliko Dangote for mobilizing private sector support in the fight.

a4716.speaker: Dr. Iziaq Adekunle Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a4716.speech: Called on Nigerians to "take personal responsibility" by sleeping under mosquito nets, maintaining clean environments, and seeking early diagnosis and treatment.

a4745.speaker: Cassiel Ato Forson, Ghana’s Finance Minister
a4745.speech: Issued a warning, speaking at the National Economic Dialogue (NED) 2025, that Ghana’s energy sector is on the verge of a financial crisis, with cumulative shortfalls expected to exceed $9 billion by 2026 if immediate reforms are not implemented; described the power sector as highly inefficient and burdened by rising operational costs and debt ; highlighted the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) as a major area of concern, noting that it collects only 62% of the energy it purchases, with a significant portion of its revenue spent on non-essential expenditures ; revealed that in 2024 the energy sector recorded a $2.2 billion shortfall, despite government transfers of $2.1 billion between 2023 and 2024 aimed at stabilizing the industry ; said unpaid legacy arrears in the energy sector stood at $1.3 billion at the end of 2022, with annual cumulative sector shortfalls reaching $2.2 billion in 2024.

a4745.speaker: Cassiel Ato Forson, Ghana’s Finance Minister (2025 budget statement presented to Parliament on March 11, 2025)
a4745.speech: Indicated that in 2024 the Ministry of Finance supported the energy sector with payments of approximately GH¢20.8 billion, and suggested that these funds could have been allocated to job creation and development programmes, such as road construction, schools, and hospitals, had the energy sector’s inefficiencies been addressed.

a4745.speaker: Cassiel Ato Forson, Ghana’s Finance Minister
a4745.speech: “Fixing the sector requires bold measures,” emphasizing the need for reforms in tariff structures, improved revenue collection, and increased investment in renewable energy to ensure the sector’s financial sustainability.

a4769.speaker: Dr. Fahd bin Hassan Al-Aqran, President of the Saudi Press Agency (SPA)
a4769.speech: Affirmed that the future of news agencies is very large given the technical development the media is currently witnessing, which news agencies have sensed and kept pace with ; Said that changing the negative mental image of the agencies is among the goals news agencies must work on, because of the tremendous speed of the media, by strengthening relations with other media outlets ; Stressed that news agencies are the main source of news and that through them news is broadcast in different ways, that news agencies have a great opportunity in the future to reach their goals thanks to their geographic spread and journalistic formats, and that intellectual property rights are among the challenges facing news agencies.

a4769.speaker: Abdullah Abdulkarim, Acting Executive Director of the News Content Sector, Emirates News Agency (WAM)
a4769.speech: Explained that crises and rumours have contributed to news agencies regaining their natural standing, which confirms that news agencies must work on defining their future goals ; Affirmed that news agencies have recently been able to harness technology in their favour and keep pace with the rapid changes in the media, noting that the Emirates News Agency has sought through its new strategy to strengthen its relationship with major regional and global media institutions, in addition to its current digital transformation.

a4769.speaker: Virgin Ajti, Editor-in-Chief of the Daily Tribune newspaper
a4769.speech: Explained that news agencies have begun to offer distinctive news services, stressing that it is important to deal with the abundance of journalists, which must be matched by a large volume of innovation, that news is a service and not a product, that news agencies bear a great responsibility in confronting the fake news that has become widespread, and that it is important to develop news agencies' news content.

a4769.speaker: Vasily Pushkov, Director of International Cooperation at the Sputnik agency
a4769.speech: Stated that media materials take many different forms through which news agencies craft these materials with full reliability so they reach the public free of falsification and rumour ; Said that society is very interested in varied and diverse news and that news agencies have been able to keep pace with all these changes and meet society's need to follow the news ; Stressed that news agencies must work for one another, so as to create a large news network providing a professional and reliable chain for producing news material.

a4773.speaker: Colonel-Major (Medical) Garba Hakimi, Minister of Public Health, Population and Social Affairs of Niger
a4773.speech: Declared on Thursday 30 January 2025 the end of onchocerciasis transmission in Niger ; Declared that this “meeting crowns several years of manifold efforts in the fight against this disfiguring disease which in the past caused several thousand cases of blindness and a major economic and social disaster in the affected communities”, explaining that onchocerciasis, or river blindness, was rife around certain watercourses in Niger – the Diamangou, the Sirba, the Mekrou, the Tapoa and the Goroubi – and affected the populations of the health districts of Téra, Bankilaré, Gotheye, Say, Torodi, Kollo, Boboye, Falmeye, Dioundiou and Gaya ; “The epidemiological, entomological, mapping and serological assessments carried out in recent years by national and sub-regional experts have shown that Niger has reached the level of interruption of transmission of this disease,” noting that his “ministerial department has, to that end, invested itself in producing a dossier reporting the general situation of the fight against onchocerciasis in our country with the support of the members of the National Committee for the Elimination of this disease” ; “The elimination of this disease is a difficult achievement which required a collective commitment of health workers, of the community and of partners.”

a4773.speaker: Colonel-Major (Medical) Garba Hakimi, Minister of Public Health of Niger
a4773.speech: Congratulated “the Programme for the efforts made over more than 15 years to provide the scientific proof of the elimination of this disease in Niger, but also the President and the members of the onchocerciasis elimination committee, all the health workers, the customary and religious leaders, and the communities” ; “I make it my pleasant duty, in the name of the highest authorities of our country, foremost among them His Excellency Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland, Head of State, and the Prime Minister Mr Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine, to salute and thank all the actors who have invested themselves in the fight against onchocerciasis in Niger.”

a4773.speaker: President of the onchocerciasis elimination committee in Niger (unnamed)
a4773.speech: Told the Minister and the audience that “our country, Niger, abounds in intelligence and in skills in every field, which must be trusted”, saluting “the trust placed in this onchocerciasis elimination committee in our country” ; “This committee is made up of a team of women and men who worked effectively under the responsibility of a coordinator who has a sense of teamwork, a man of integrity, patriotic, hardworking and disinterested” ; said “insecurity, precisely in these areas, somewhat delayed, among other things, the attainment of this noble objective. But thanks to the patriotism and the courage of our blackfly catchers (the flies that are the reservoir of the parasite), sometimes at the risk of their lives from the risk of attacks by terrorists and also by wild animals – but thanks to the courage of our catchers the mission continued.”

a4773.speaker: President of the onchocerciasis elimination committee in Niger (unnamed)
a4773.speech: Said the Committee benefited from “the appreciable and multifaceted support of partners, traditionally mainly in the field of public health. This contributed significantly and allowed our country to attain this honourable objective”, citing among other partners the WHO, USAID, HKI, the END FUND and FHI 360, whose “sincere and disinterested support we hope for in the post-elimination surveillance of the disease” ; “Mr Minister, after your declaration, one can say that there is something to be proud of, to be Nigerien, and this too we think is a quest for sovereignty obtained through our work for our country, which deserves the adherence of the whole Nigerien nation.”

a4773.speaker: Dr Casimir Manengu, WHO Representative in Niger
a4773.speech: Said “Niger has waged an effective fight against this disease for decades, with the support of all stakeholders, notably the WHO through its onchocerciasis control programme, the ‘OCP’ (Onchocerciasis Control Programme)”, stressing that “this programme provided the necessary assistance to the eleven endemic West African countries in the fight against this disease for 15 years (from 1974 to 1989); these countries then took over through their national onchocerciasis devolution programmes, thus embarking on the path to eliminating this disease” ; declared the result is “on the one hand irrefutable proof that the elimination of transmission of human onchocerciasis is possible in Africa, and on the other hand a significant contribution by Niger to the main objective of the 2021-2030 global road map for neglected tropical diseases, which aims for 100 countries to eliminate at least one neglected tropical disease by 2030 compared with 2020” ; said Niger contributes “to the attainment of the global target relating to onchocerciasis” and underlined “the importance of strengthening integrated disease surveillance in Niger to maintain the gains”, calling on all technical and financial partners to support Niger in its efforts to improve the health and well-being of its population.

a4792.speaker: The Vatican
a4792.speech: Has announced that the funeral of Pope Francis will be held on Saturday, April 26, at 10:00 am local time in St. Peter's Square.

a4792.speaker: Pope Francis
a4792.speech: Had requested a simpler funeral, eschewing the traditional pomp and ceremony, and had specified that he wanted to be buried in the Santa Maria Maggiore basilica, not in St. Peter's Basilica, saying "The Vatican is the home of my last service, not my eternal home".

a4792.speaker: Guo Jiakun, Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson
a4792.speech: Expressed condolences on behalf of China, highlighting Pope Francis' efforts to improve relations between China and the Vatican.

a4836.speaker: Assessment of Cabo Verde's Emergency Preparedness and Response system (diagnostic report)
a4836.speech: found that the system was, at the end of 2019, in the early stages of development, with a low overall score compared with international standards; many fundamental elements were simply not in place, leading the assessors to classify the system as structurally fragile and highly vulnerable to human, social and economic losses in the event of a disaster.

a4836.speaker: Assessment of Cabo Verde's Emergency Preparedness and Response system (diagnostic report)
a4836.speech: identified the absence of an effective Information Management System as one of the most critical gaps, and considered the non-existence of mass evacuation plans for islands such as Fogo and Santo Antao alarming given the real risk of volcanic eruptions and other natural disasters; revealed the lack of shelters and spaces prepared to receive displaced populations and the weakness of emergency response infrastructure; concluded that municipalities lack properly structured civil protection services with qualified human resources and adequate equipment.

a4836.speaker: Assessment of Cabo Verde's Emergency Preparedness and Response system (diagnostic report)
a4836.speech: acknowledges important advances, above all in the legal and institutional framework, noting that Cabo Verde has basic civil protection legislation including the Civil Protection Framework Law (2012) and the National Contingency Plan (2010), although many provisions have not been implemented; the highest score was in the criterion of legislative responsibility, even if considered insufficient.

a4836.speaker: Assessment of Cabo Verde's Emergency Preparedness and Response system (diagnostic report)
a4836.speech: identified a positive point in fighting urban fires and technical rescue, but warned of the lack of clear selection criteria and of standards on minimum staffing and equipment requirements, which undermines the effectiveness of fire brigades, noting that in some cases serving firefighters do not meet the physical standards needed.

a4836.speaker: Assessment of Cabo Verde's Emergency Preparedness and Response system (diagnostic report)
a4836.speech: underlined the absence of structured international coordination for support in emergencies, a serious gap for a small island state exposed to multiple risks; although Cabo Verde has access to cooperation mechanisms such as those of the European Union, the lack of internal protocols and clear coordination mechanisms means external aid is not mobilised efficiently.

a4836.speaker: Authors of the diagnosis
a4836.speech: point out that in terms of community involvement there are isolated good practices, led by organisations such as the Cabo Verde Red Cross, but that these initiatives are not sufficient to create a national culture of preparedness, with community education, drills and training of local leaders practically absent or incipient.

a4836.speaker: Assessment of Cabo Verde's Emergency Preparedness and Response system (diagnostic report)
a4836.speech: recommends an urgent strengthening of the Emergency Preparedness and Response system, prioritising an integrated national information management system, inter-island evacuation plans and clear standards for municipal civil protection services, plus continuous training of professionals, more national-municipal coordination and greater involvement of civil society and the private sector; concludes that the distance between the legal framework and operational reality is still great.

a4836.speaker: Specialists (authors of the assessment)
a4836.speech: say that turning strategies into concrete actions will be fundamental to reducing the country's vulnerability and protecting the development gains achieved in recent decades.

a4934.speaker: 2024 report on imports of goods from abroad (Tanzania)
a4934.speech: shows large imports of industrial equipment, reflecting the growth of the country's industrial sector: a total of Sh43.076 trillion was spent on importing various goods, with industrial equipment leading at Sh11 trillion, followed by iron and its products (Sh7.02 trillion); the industrial sector has become an important pillar of economic development, creating large demand for plant, machinery and other industrial equipment.

a4934.speaker: Economists (unnamed)
a4934.speech: explained that this increase is directly related to the Government's efforts to grow the industrial economy through development projects and investment policies.

a4934.speaker: Dr Dickson Pastory, lecturer in economics at the College of Business Education (CBE)
a4934.speech: said: "Because of the good environment put in place by the Government, foreign investors have been attracted, so the increase in industrial investors has led to an increase in the importation of industrial equipment." ; said that among the things that stimulated the country's manufacturing sector is the change in investment policy, which contributed to some industries being exempted from taxes and levies in order to increase investment.

a4934.speaker: Dr Thobiasi Swai, economic analyst
a4934.speech: said: "On the whole it appears that industries have increased in the country, so an increase in the importation of goods is inevitable in order to enable the production of manufactured goods."

a4934.speaker: Balozi Morwa, lecturer at Mbeya Catholic University
a4934.speech: warned about the effects arising from this increase, saying there is a need for such equipment to be produced domestically in order to reduce the heavy use of foreign currency: "The increase in imports shows that we have no production of industrial equipment; it is important to think of ways of building the capacity to produce this equipment within the country. This will help reduce the use of foreign currency and strengthen the domestic economy further."

a4934.speaker: Gilead Teri, Director of the Tanzania Investment Centre (TIC)
a4934.speech: said that in the period January to December 2024 the Tanzania Investment Centre registered a total of 901 projects, compared with 526 projects registered in the same period in 2023, and that these projects attracted capital of Sh23.5 trillion compared with Sh14.44 trillion in January-December 2023.

a5057.speaker: Clemens Kapuuo, Herero chief and deputy chairman of the National Convention (statement)
a5057.speech: In a long statement, sharply rejects the attacks directed against him and the National Convention by SWAPO; his reply, copied to the UN Secretary-General, the UN Commissioner for Namibia, the ambassadors of the United States and England and the Federal Government in Bonn, reads: “South West Africa is a country that is still under colonial rule. The colonisation of South West Africa, which continues to this day, began with Germany. At the beginning of the 20th century, when Germany sent troops to South West Africa, a bitter war took place between the Germans and the African tribes in South West Africa... Under the infamous extermination order of the German administration under Mr von Trotha, all men, women and children were to be killed. As a result of the extermination order, more than half of the entire Herero tribe was wiped out.”

a5057.speaker: Filemon Elifas, Chief Minister of Owambo
a5057.speech: Issued an appeal to the Ovambo people in which he pointed to the importance of the elections to the Legislative Council held from 13 to 17 January; in his address he also appealed to employers outside Owambo to give Ovambos entitled to vote the opportunity to cast their ballots, with a special appeal to farmers to bring their farm workers to the nearest polling station ; emphasised the autonomy of Owambo and calls on all Ovambos to make use of their right to vote, asking employers for corresponding assistance.

a5057.speaker: SWAPO
a5057.speech: Argues that an election must be held throughout South West Africa on the principle of one man, one vote, and not in individual ethnic areas; has refused to put forward candidates and is endeavouring, at least in the south, to propagate a boycott of the election.

a5057.speaker: Police spokesman (Frankfurt police, unnamed)
a5057.speech: Reported that the singing “monks” – among them eight women – did comply after an hour with the police's request to disperse, but that when they then drove with their three minibuses in the direction of police headquarters they were stopped in the city centre and taken to headquarters for a check of their personal details; they are accused of violating the Assembly Act.

a5057.speaker: Antonio de Almeida Santos, Portuguese Minister for the Overseas Territories
a5057.speech: Told the Reuters agency that the success of the Angola conference depends more on the cooperation of the three Angolan forces than on the goodwill of the Portuguese government; that there can be no doubt about the intentions and the impartiality of the Portuguese government in seeking a selfless solution for Angola.

a5135.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5135.speech: Delivering the keynote address at the launch ceremony in Accra on July 2, 2025, declared: “The path is going to be challenging, but we will succeed. And we will succeed with discipline, coordination and shared purpose.” He described the 24-hour Agenda as a national reset and a bold step toward self-reliance, inclusivity and prosperity, and as the beginning of a new model of economic development, one grounded in productivity, powered by the private sector and coordinated by the state.

a5135.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5135.speech: Explained that the vision was inspired by deep reflection during and after his previous administration, and described Ghana's economic model as one trapped in a cycle of unequal exchange: “We ship cocoa, gold, timber and oil abroad, only to repurchase them as chocolates, jewelry, furniture and fuel at a far greater cost. This model does not serve our people. It generates foreign jobs and funds foreign healthcare and education systems.”

a5135.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5135.speech: Emphasized that the 24-hour Agenda is not merely about working longer hours, but about unleashing productivity, expanding opportunity and boosting exports, calling it a “coherent, integrated and multi-sectoral national strategy”; on the eight sub-programmes he explained: “These are not just names. They represent a structural rethinking of how we target job-rich, export-oriented sectors and build forward and backward linkages across the economy.”

a5135.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5135.speech: Announced on the Border Economic Corridor: “We will recreate over 2 million hectares of high-intensity agriculture under GROW24. We will establish agro-industrial parks for textiles, pharmaceuticals, and food processing, and tourism clusters along the lake under SHOW24” ; “We will turn the lake into a central transport highway that connects north to south, east to west under CONNECT24.” He said this was the realisation of Kwame Nkrumah's dream of an integrated economic corridor powered by Akosombo, long overdue for revival.

a5135.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5135.speech: On funding, emphasized that the government's role will be catalytic, not dominant: “Government will facilitate, not control. Enterprise financing will come from commercial banks, development finance institutions, and blended instruments. Government funds will be used primarily for bulk infrastructure and to support a soon-to-be-autonomous 24-hour Plus Authority.” He announced that FUND24 will be tasked with addressing capital access issues, providing credit guarantees, and avoiding breach of Ghana's fiscal responsibilities to international lenders, and said the authority will evolve into a permanent institution reporting directly to the President — not just him, but “the next President and the next after that.”

a5135.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5135.speech: Issued a call to national duty, inviting labour unions, the private sector, traditional leaders, youth groups, civil society, and development partners to fully embrace the 24-hour agenda: “This programme is for Ghana's future. It is a national strategy to ensure inclusive growth, export expansion, job creation, and structural transformation. Ghana belongs to all of us. The work of transformation must be the task of all of us.”

a5297.speaker: Alfredo Maxlhaieie, administrator of the Mossuril district
a5297.speech: "At the moment, around 16 houses are under construction. It is a gradual process that involves not only the craftsmen, but also the population itself, who are being trained in this construction process. But in total, 69 houses will be built."

a5297.speaker: Alfredo Maxlhaieie, administrator of the Mossuril district
a5297.speech: According to Maxlhaieie, Cyclone Jude affected more than 200,000 people in Mossuril, corresponding to 26,000 families who continue to receive assistance from various partners in their areas of residence, "both in terms of food supplies, agriculture and water supply".

a5425.speaker: Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a5425.speech: Announced on 1 April that the ceremony handing over Russian humanitarian aid took place in Niamey on 26 March with the participation of the Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Niger and Mali, Igor Gromyko.

a5425.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a5425.speech: According to WFP, the Russian aid will make it possible to supply the most vulnerable, including refugees, for three months.

a5466.speaker: Professor Tahir Mamman, Minister of Education
a5466.speech: Recently directed the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) and the National Examinations Council (NECO), both institutions that conduct the Senior School Certificate Examinations (SSCE), to reject applicants who are less than 18 years of age ; in his earlier attempt to enforce it, Mamman had instructed the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) to ensure only students who were 18 years and above sat for the University Tertiary Matriculation Examinations (UTME) for admission into Nigerian universities in 2024, but he backed down after his instruction was opposed by stakeholders.

a5466.speaker: C.O. Taiwo, in his work 'The Nigerian Education System'
a5466.speech: Articulates the objectives of primary education to include: "the development of sound standards of individual conduct and behaviour; an understanding of the community and of what is of value for its development, and of the contribution which the individual can make to the community; the development of a lively curiosity leading to a desire for knowledge about the immediate environment and the world outside; permanent literacy; and the acquisition of some skill of hand and a recognition of the value of manual work."

a5478.speaker: United States Embassy in Juba (press statement)
a5478.speech: Said it is working with humanitarian partners - through the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) - to help address the ongoing cholera outbreak in South Sudan ; said it is providing funding to UN agencies and medical charity MSF to deliver emergency water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services and provide life-saving medical care, with other priority measures including supporting vaccination campaigns, provision of treatment kits and diagnostic tests, and raising public awareness ; "This funding will enhance public awareness campaigns on the dangers of cholera and prevention measures such as safe water use, proper food handling, and good hygiene practices." ; "It will also strengthen WASH interventions and equip health officials with critical resources to treat cases effectively." ; reaffirmed Washington's support to the South Sudanese people "during this challenging time", adding that the assistance will save lives and help prevent the spread of cholera in vulnerable communities.

a5478.speaker: U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID)
a5478.speech: On December 29, USAID said it delivered more than 2 million Aquatab water purification tablets as part of the humanitarian response to the ongoing cholera outbreak. The tablets, it said, will treat six million gallons of water, providing safe drinking water to communities most affected by the outbreak.

a5478.speaker: United States Embassy in Juba (press statement)
a5478.speech: "We renew our call on South Sudan's transitional government to start using public revenue to address its people's health needs, provide other basic services, and to pay public sector salaries for health workers, other civil servants, and security personnel."

a5574.speaker: Six sources familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a5574.speech: Told Reuters that President Donald Trump's administration on Tuesday moved to reinstate at least six recently cancelled U.S. foreign aid programs for emergency food assistance; five sources said Lewin asked to restore awards to the World Food Programme in Lebanon, Syria, Somalia, Jordan, Iraq and Ecuador; two sources said the administration has also resumed four awards to the International Organization for Migration in the Pacific region; two sources said the decision to restore some aid followed pressure from inside the administration and from Congress.

a5574.speaker: Jeremy Lewin, USAID Acting Deputy Administrator
a5574.speech: Asked staff in an internal email to reverse the terminations ; "Sorry for all the back and forth on awards. There are a lot of stakeholders and we need to do better about balancing these competing interests - that's my fault and I take responsibility."

a5574.speaker: Reuters
a5574.speech: Reported on Monday that the Trump administration had ended life-saving aid programs for more than a dozen countries including Afghanistan, Yemen, Somalia and Syria, totalling over $1.3 billion.

a5574.speaker: Stand Up For Aid (advocacy group of current and former U.S. officials)
a5574.speech: According to the group, WFP contracts cancelled on Lewin's orders last weekend for Lebanon, Syria, Somalia and Jordan totalled more than $463 million.

a5574.speaker: US State Department
a5574.speech: Said the waivers granted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio to many of the terminated programs did not reflect a final decision.

a5574.speaker: US State Department
a5574.speech: Did not immediately respond to a request for comment about restoring the awards.

a5574.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a5574.speech: Said on Monday that the U.S. notified the organization it was eliminating emergency food assistance funding in 14 countries, warning: "If implemented, this could amount to a death sentence for millions of people facing extreme hunger and starvation."

a5574.speaker: Tammy Bruce, State Department spokesperson
a5574.speech: Told reporters on Tuesday that the United States had concerns that WFP funding for Yemen and Afghanistan was benefiting the Houthis and the Taliban ; "There were a few programs that were cut in other countries that were not meant to be cut that have been rolled back and put into place," adding that the administration remains committed to foreign aid.

a5574.speaker: Senate Foreign Relations Committee Democrats (letter to Marco Rubio)
a5574.speech: Wrote a letter to Rubio on Tuesday regarding plans to restructure the State Department, including by folding in USAID, which they said was "unconstitutional, illegal, unjustified, damaging, and inefficient."

a5800.speaker: Economic analysts
a5800.speech: stressed that to counter its effects will demand great determination in 2021, 2022 and beyond ; said that planning for this challenging global future needs to start right now, even though we do not yet know the full degree of the pain that the world's citizens and their economies are set to endure in the immediate period ahead.

a5800.speaker: David Malpass, World Bank President
a5800.speech: estimates that up to 150 million people are being plunged into extreme poverty this year, taking the global total to well above 800 million.

a5800.speaker: IMF
a5800.speech: forecasts that the world's economy will recover significantly in 2021 from its near-depression 2020 levels; the economic rebound will be due to the demise of the virus and the abundance of vaccines and effective treatments.

a5800.speaker: Frank Vogl, Co-founder of Transparency International and author of “Waging War on Corruption: Inside the Movement Fighting the Abuse of Power”
a5800.speech: stated that the great unraveling embraces a failure of multilateral strategic decision-making at the highest levels. The Trump administration has led the charge as the great disrupter – attacking the World Health Organization, deriding the World Trade Organization, and failing to lead on multilateral financial responses.

a5800.speaker: Frank Vogl, Co-founder of Transparency International
a5800.speech: noted that the onset of the global financial crisis in September 2008 saw the convening in less than two months of a Group of 20 summit meeting to determine collective international action. This year, the Group of Seven has been in hiding. The Finance Ministers of the G20 have only met to take minimal measures to kick the can down the road. All they did was call for short-term deferrals in debt repayments by the world's poorest countries.

a5800.speaker: Frank Vogl, Co-founder of Transparency International
a5800.speech: stressed that the immediate multilateral response to this crisis has been swift: Giant lending programs launched by the International Monetary Fund, and rapid disbursing loans and grants from the World Bank. Debt is being piled upon debt across the universe.

a5800.speaker: Frank Vogl, Co-founder of Transparency International
a5800.speech: stated that the financial resources of the IMF will need to be hugely expanded. It has to develop systems to enable countries to stretch out their official debt servicing in return to being willing to be open to forceful IMF monitoring of exactly how the aid funds are used. The G7, for its part, needs to hold a special meeting to find ways to convince China to become part of the international “Paris Club” of official creditors and agree to making transparent its loan arrangements with dozens of countries.

a5800.speaker: Lex Rieffel, Nonresident Fellow with the East Asia Program at the Stimson Center
a5800.speech: stated that public spending deficits are reaching record highs in many countries. However, because interest rates are close to record lows, central bankers tend to be relaxed about this... tens of millions of pensioners who depend on yields from their fixed income investments are likely to face financial hardship. Not a single government has yet addressed the financial distress of the elderly in high-income countries. This is a giant problem that may take a toll for years to come.

a5800.speaker: Lex Rieffel, Nonresident Fellow, Stimson Center
a5800.speech: argued that with the pandemic destroying economies, emerging market countries desperately need more cash to service their existing outstanding debts. China, for its part, is renegotiating some of its deals, but keeping all details secret. The 75 lowest income countries are being allowed by the G20 to defer debt servicing until June 2021. In contrast, the commercial creditors to these countries are not being generous. Inevitably, IMF loans are being recycled by the recipient countries to pay off the Chinese and commercial creditors.

a5800.speaker: Lex Rieffel, Nonresident Fellow, Stimson Center
a5800.speech: According to him, the G20, the IMF and the World Bank at the global level, just like the EU and U.S. authorities at the regional and national levels, are pouring unprecedented amounts of money at the immediate COVID 19 challenge, hoping that somehow there will never be a day of reckoning. These emergency responses are not only understandable, but laudable. There are no alternatives.

a5894.speaker: Professor Ntobeko Ntusi, president of the South African Medical Research Council (SAMRC), writing in the journal Nature
a5894.speech: Made the argument for increased independence in Africa and the global south, and for clarity on longer-term strategies for greater self-sufficiency in HIV responses as donor-funded models look increasingly precarious.

a5894.speaker: Some beneficiaries of US-funded projects (anonymous, speaking on condition of anonymity)
a5894.speech: Told Spotlight that South Africa should have been better prepared and not caught off guard to be left in the position it now finds itself in. They were speaking on condition of anonymity, given the risk of public comments jeopardising their prospects of having their funding restored.

a5894.speaker: USAID website
a5894.speech: According to USAID’s website, it invested $5.6 billion (roughly R100 billion at the current rand/dollar exchange rate) between 2004 and 2020 towards the prevention and treatment of HIV and TB in South Africa.

a5894.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5894.speech: Since taking office, Trump has slated USAID as “corrupt” and run by “radical left lunatics”.

a5894.speaker: United States mission in South Africa
a5894.speech: Confirmed that some Pepfar-funded services could continue in the country, subject to some relatively strict limitations and with no assurances of longer-term support.

a5894.speaker: Bhekisisa (reporting)
a5894.speech: As is clear from reporting by Bhekisisa, the process to get at least some funding to flow again to Pepfar-supported projects is not straightforward.

a5894.speaker: White House media note of 29 January
a5894.speech: “The previously announced 90-day pause and review of US foreign aid is already paying dividends to our country and our people. We are rooting out waste. We are blocking woke programmes. And we are exposing activities that run contrary to our national interests. None of this would be possible if these programmes remained on autopilot.”

a5894.speaker: US Mission in South Africa (FAQ published 10 February)
a5894.speech: According to the FAQ, they have been communicating with the South African government, though it is not clear when this happened.

a5894.speaker: Dr Aaron Motsoaledi, South African Health Minister
a5894.speech: Told Parliament’s portfolio committee on 5 February that he had not received any official communication from the US government on the matter.

a5894.speaker: Dr Aaron Motsoaledi, South African Health Minister (presentation to Parliament)
a5894.speech: Figures from Motsoaledi’s presentation showed that in 2023/24, Pepfar funding to South Africa’s health department amounted to 17% of its spending on HIV, totalling R4.6 billion for staffing and R2.9 billion for running costs for NGOs, with Pepfar focusing on the 27 districts with the highest disease burden ; said that since Trump’s executive order came into place, the health department had hosted a meeting with the provincial leads on HIV and TB, conducted assessments on the immediate impacts of the executive order, met with people living with HIV and engaged with the South African National AIDS Council (Sanac) to finalise a sustainability framework. He did not give details of contingencies or next steps in his presentation to Parliament.

a5894.speaker: South African Department of Health (non-response)
a5894.speech: The health department did not respond to Spotlight’s questions on contingencies, details of next steps to fill the funding gaps, or how capacity and resources will be redirected to avert catastrophe.

a5894.speaker: Collective of activist organisations, including the Health Justice Initiative, Section27, the Cancer Alliance, Treatment Action Campaign, Sweat, PSAM and the African Alliance
a5894.speech: Pressed the Department of Health to create an “urgent co-ordinated emergency plan”, and increase the budget to avert a looming disaster ; highlighted that despite the announcement by the Trump administration that some NGOs could apply for a waiver, many have had no practical way to do so without ways to communicate with their USAID contacts ; extended their appeal to protecting the work of academic and clinical research in the fields of HIV, TB and cervical cancer, which will also be affected by the funding freeze.

a5894.speaker: Professor Linda-Gail Bekker, CEO of the Desmond Tutu Health Foundation
a5894.speech: Said Trump’s actions put in jeopardy the goal to finally have epidemic control of HIV – and right at the final hurdles. “We have made amazing progress. And thank you to Pepfar, that helped us to get this far, but the work is not over. For the US to pull out at this point is a massive loss of investment; it’s also regression. It’s like getting to the end of a book but having the last chapters torn out before you can read it.” ; said Pepfar funding has made it possible to build a formidable cohort of lay and professional people trained and dedicated to their roles that supported public healthcare in the most critical ways: “These are individuals who distribute antiretrovirals, distribute pre-exposure prophylaxis, find and trace individuals who’ve been lost to care. They take services into communities, to outside of the health facilities, and made the effort to go the last mile to find those individuals - that is how you close down the epidemic.” ; “HIV and TB track together all the time, and an HIV epidemic that is once again out of control almost certainly means what will follow is a TB epidemic that is out of control.”

a5894.speaker: Dr Andy Gray, University of KwaZulu-Natal
a5894.speech: Said Trump has created an “unreal world”. “People are being held to ransom; and people are scared.” “We have always been used to the oscillation between the United States’ Republican and Democratic administrations; things may be a little uncomfortable, or there may be some disruption, but not this ‘let’s burn down the house’ approach taken by the Trump administration.” “There is no consideration of human rights or for human beings anywhere in the world, including America”, also pointing out that the CDC has, for the first time in 60 years, been instructed to cease publishing weekly mortality and morbidity data, despite a breakout of avian flu (H5) in the country.

a5894.speaker: Dr Andy Gray, University of KwaZulu-Natal
a5894.speech: Said South Africa’s strategic health response in the wake of this crisis should be to shift from a donor-funded model, though his concern is that with a stretched South African purse and competing priorities the HIV response will slip down the list; said better self-sufficiency comes from eliminating waste, investing in employing the right people in the right jobs, as well as investing in efficient systems; added that the National Treasury will have to redirect money for the interim shortfall left by the US funding freeze, and provinces will have to step up by getting their houses in order; warned that South Africa should ready itself for the “worst-case scenario” once the 90-day review period is up.

a5894.speaker: Nelson Dlamini, head of communications of the South African National AIDS Council (Sanac)
a5894.speech: Said they have been left in a position of not being able to engage publicly because they haven’t had any direct communication with Pepfar and USAID representatives based in Pretoria. “Pepfar is a government-to-government agreement, and there ought to be official communication with the government of South Africa, so we know what this means for our working relationship, but nothing has been forthcoming.” “Sanac is a co-ordinator, so we have to still coordinate. We are engaging in the background with relevant structures, but we can’t say we are doing X, Y, Z till we have a sit down with Pepfar.”

a6046.speaker: Mulambo Haimbe, Zambian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a6046.speech: Disclosed, addressing Parliament, that Zambia risks being added to the United States travel ban list unless key issues related to immigration enforcement, passport integrity, and international cooperation are swiftly resolved, and said the Government had received formal diplomatic communication from the U.S. indicating that Zambia is under review for potential travel restrictions if concerns raised are not addressed within a specified period ; “We have received official correspondence from the Government of the United States indicating the consideration of imposing travel restrictions on Zambia” ; “The concerns raised include the security and integrity of our passport systems, enforcement of removal orders for Zambian nationals living irregularly in the U.S., and deficiencies in information sharing between our governments.”

a6046.speaker: Mulambo Haimbe, Zambian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a6046.speech: Warned that the implications of such restrictions would be far-reaching and could negatively affect Zambia's image globally: “If Zambia is placed on the travel ban list, we risk having our legitimate travelers who include students, businesspeople, athletes, and government officials face increased visa scrutiny or outright denial. This could send the wrong signal to investors and partners, suggesting Zambia is failing to meet international compliance obligations” ; explained that a travel ban could create complications for Zambians already residing in the United States, especially those with irregular immigration status: “Such individuals may face legal uncertainties, potential deportation, or barriers to regularizing their status” ; said the travel ban threat also risks interrupting bilateral technical and development cooperation that depends on free movement of personnel between the two countries.

a6046.speaker: Mulambo Haimbe, Zambian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a6046.speech: Emphasised that the Government had moved quickly and decisively to respond: “We are taking this matter very seriously. We have initiated a comprehensive review of our passport security measures, and we are enhancing our systems to align with international best practices” ; noted that Zambia is working closely with the U.S. through diplomatic channels: “The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, together with our embassy in Washington, D.C., has engaged the U.S. State Department and the Department of Homeland Security. Our goal is to ensure Zambia is removed from the review list within the 60-day window that has been provided” ; updated the House on a recent high-level meeting with U.S. Embassy officials held on June 24: “The discussions were candid and constructive. We agreed on a framework for monthly consultative meetings to ensure sustained dialogue and cooperation” ; revealed that the U.S. had committed to sharing data on Zambian nationals who had overstayed their visas, and said “In a positive development, the U.S. has offered to assist Zambia with technical support aimed at digitising and securing our passports and national registration cards.”

a6046.speaker: Mulambo Haimbe, Zambian Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a6046.speech: Assured the nation that there is no fall-out between the US and Zambia and that the threat gives both countries an opportunity to strengthen their long bilateral ties; was quick to clarify that the situation should not be misinterpreted as a diplomatic fallout: “This development does not signify a rupture in Zambia–U.S. relations. Rather, it is an opportunity for us to strengthen our institutions, improve civil registration, and reaffirm our commitment to global cooperation” ; assured Parliament that the government would continue engaging all relevant stakeholders transparently: “We are making progress, and we are confident that through our coordinated and proactive approach, we will address the concerns and safeguard Zambia's international standing.”

a6046.speaker: Government of the United States (formal diplomatic communication / official correspondence)
a6046.speech: Indicated that Zambia is under review for potential travel restrictions if the concerns raised – the security and integrity of Zambia's passport systems, enforcement of removal orders for Zambian nationals living irregularly in the U.S., and deficiencies in information sharing – are not addressed within a specified 60-day period.

a6078.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Namibian Minister of Health and Social Services
a6078.speech: Says all U.S. funds allocated to local health programs, including HIV/AIDS initiatives, are accounted for ; “Funds were advanced before the order took effect, meaning work will continue. We anticipate a positive review, and there is nothing suggesting Namibia is non-compliant with U.S. expectations. We are cautiously optimistic that operations will continue as usual.”

a6078.speaker: Namibian Ministry of Health and Social Services
a6078.speech: Assures that program rollouts remain unaffected for now.

a6078.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Namibian Minister of Health and Social Services
a6078.speech: Reaffirms Namibia's accountability, stating that U.S. funds are managed by American agencies, not the Health Ministry: “The funds are not handled by the Ministry but by U.S.-established agencies. There is no indication of mismanagement on Namibia's part.”

a6078.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Namibian Minister of Health and Social Services
a6078.speech: Is confident Namibia's programs remain sustainable: “When we launched malaria, TB, and HIV/AIDS programs, they were government-led initiatives. They receive annual parliamentary appropriations, ensuring sustainability. Unlike some countries where donor funding covers 90% of costs, Namibia is not in that position.”

a6091.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6091.speech: warned Zelensky against refusing the rare metals deal; told journalists that Volodymyr Zelensky is about to back out of the rare metals deal. "Zelensky is trying to back out of the rare earths deal and if he does, he will have problems, big, big problems."

a6091.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6091.speech: also stressed that Volodymyr Zelensky still wants Ukraine to become a member of NATO. However, according to Donald Trump, it "will never become one." "He [Zelensky] understands that."

a6091.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6091.speech: shared his thoughts on tariffs against Russia. He would "certainly not" want to impose additional duties on Russian products, but if they were introduced, "it would not be good for it [Russia]." He recalled that the United States had imposed such duties on Venezuela and that this had had "a very strong impact." "You know that all the ships have left, many of them have left. They dropped the pipes right into the ocean and left."

a6091.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6091.speech: did not indicate a deadline for Russia to accept a ceasefire in the Ukraine conflict. The American leader also said he was convinced that Russian President Vladimir Putin "wants to make a deal" on settling the Ukrainian conflict. Asked about possible Russian stalling on establishing a ceasefire, Donald Trump replied that he was not convinced of it.

a6091.speaker: Iaroslav Jelezniak, deputy in the Verkhovna Rada (Ukrainian parliament)
a6091.speech: said that under the new agreement, Kyiv would be obliged to transfer mineral revenues to a special fund, while American aid from 2022 onward would be counted as the United States' contribution.

a6091.speaker: Kirill Dmitriev, director of the Russian Direct Investment Fund
a6091.speech: reported that some American companies have already shown interest in these [rare earth metals] projects. According to him, this is an important area of cooperation.

a6182.speaker: Fars news agency
a6182.speech: Reported that Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and several other officials were lightly wounded in the legs as a result of an Israeli air strike on a meeting of the Supreme National Security Council in Tehran; revealed that the president of the Islamic Republic and other senior officials were forced to flee the building where the meeting was being held through an emergency hatch; according to Fars, Israel reportedly fired at least six missiles to block the escape routes and the strike may have been coordinated with the help of an Israeli spy network.

a6182.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6182.speech: Announced that Israel and Iran had agreed to a complete ceasefire, which came into force on 24 June.

a6182.speaker: Official data (Iranian)
a6182.speech: According to official data, 1,060 Iranians were victims of the conflict, with more than 5,000 wounded.

a6189.speaker: Subeta Mutelo, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Permanent Secretary
a6189.speech: Said the change in the health market landscape was an indication of business opportunities in the sector that health entrepreneurs could exploit responsibly and ethically; said there was a notable emergence of private laboratories/diagnostic centres, clinics, hospitals, and pharmacies beyond the line of rail as witnessed in North-Western and Eastern provinces; noted that supporting quality healthcare delivery among private healthcare facilities could be attained through sound business management practices ; "My ministry understands the various challenges that entrepreneurs across different sectors face. Health entrepreneurs are facing an unusual challenge of the perception that healthcare is a public good." ; "Facilities are set up by founders that are clinicians, who are often driven by service delivery passion. However, the healthcare market in Zambia has evolved with over a thousand retail pharmacies and over 800 private clinics and hospitals owned by locals and foreigners."

a6189.speaker: Subeta Mutelo, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Permanent Secretary
a6189.speech: On USAID: thanked USAID's unwavering commitment to strengthening the healthcare systems through clinical support and business capacity building; said that by building the capacity of Small and Medium-Sized healthcare enterprises, USAID was playing a key role in ensuring that these facilities sustainably deliver quality healthcare; urged BAP participants to use the knowledge and skills acquired through this training to lead their enterprises into a future which is sustainable and with financial growth: "As you receive your certificates today, I encourage you to apply these lessons in your daily operations. Whether it is improving financial management, ensuring compliance with regulatory standards, or accessing financing, the future of your businesses and the well-being of the communities you serve will benefit from your hard work."

a6189.speaker: Chanda Mulimansenga, Coalition Health Zambia Executive Director
